papers.title: The generalized Segal conjecture and the coalgebraic Frobenius
papers.abstract:
We prove the generalized Segal conjecture, extending work of Bergsaker and Rognes and confirming a conjecture by the author: for every finite group $G$ and every bounded-below spectrum $X$, the Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel norm $N_e^G X$ becomes Borel-complete after completion at the augmentation ideal of the Burnside ring. Equivalently, for every non-trivial finite $p$-group $G$, the proper Tate diagonal $X\to(X^{\otimes G})^{\varphi G}$ is a $p$-completion. The proof reduces to the case $X=\Fp$, established by Bergsaker and Rognes, and removes the finiteness hypotheses from their theorem by abstract manipulations.
  As an application of this result, we refine the coalgebraic Frobenius to an oriented circle action (i.e. an action of the monoidal category $B\mathbb N$) on the category of bounded-below, $p$-complete $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-coalgebras, confirming another conjecture by the author. The construction is based on Yuan's approach to Frobenius actions via partial algebraic $K$-theory.

papers.title: Equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: We construct explicit symmetric-function realizations of the torus-equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of types B and D. More precisely, we realize the extended $K$-theoretic Peterson algebras as subalgebras of a completed ring of equivariant symmetric functions and identify their Schubert classes in terms of symmetric functions. We introduce two new families of equivariant symmetric functions for each of types B and D and prove that these functions represent the classes of the structure sheaves of Schubert varieties and the ideal sheaves of their boundaries, respectively. We establish several fundamental properties of these functions, including translation factorization formulas and explicit expressions for the classes indexed by small affine Grassmannian elements. In type D, we further describe the action of the affine Dynkin diagram automorphism interchanging the two spin nodes and show how it intertwines the Schubert bases with a nontrivial transformation of the equivariant parameters.

papers.title: Higher rewriting for strong linearly distributive coherence
papers.abstract:
Rewriting is a computational method to solve word problems: deciding whether two compound expressions, or words, are equivalent with respect to a set of identities. Higher rewriting generalizes rewriting to higher-dimensional words, or cells, in higher categories.
  Following Guiraud and Malbos, we use higher rewriting to generalize Mac Lane's coherence theorem. Our result concerns strong linearly distributive categories: categories equipped with two unital tensor products related by invertible distributors. We show that in a strong linearly distributive category every formal diagram commutes.

papers.title: Local Capacity and Thresholds for Simultaneous Egyptian Fraction Packings
papers.abstract: We study pairwise disjoint sets of denominators in a common interval whose reciprocal sums are prescribed rational numbers. Put $L=\log N$ and $U=\log L$. For targets in a fixed compact subinterval of $(1/d,\infty)$ satisfying a common denominator condition, our sufficient and necessary bounds give the same first two terms in the loss from the harmonic mass of $[d,N]$, namely $U^2/(2L)+U\log U/L$. The construction also bounds the number of terms in each group. For unit targets, let $\mathfrak C_N$ be the maximum reciprocal mass compatible with the zero-residue conditions at the primes above $\sqrt N$. For all but $O(X^{11/12})$ integers $N\le X$, both the maximum number of disjoint unit sums and the largest integer representable by a single subset are equal to $\lfloor\mathfrak C_N\rfloor$. If $X_j$ denotes either the least height permitting $j$ disjoint unit sums or the least height permitting one representation of $j$, then \[ \log X_j=j-\gamma+\frac{(\log j)^2}{2j} +\frac{\log j\,\log\log j}{j} +O\!\left(\frac{\log j\,\log\log\log j}{j}\right). \]

papers.title: $E_d$-Enhancements of $L_\infty$-Algebras Associated to Secondary Polytopes
papers.abstract: We study $E_d$-enhancements of the geometric $L_\infty$-algebras associated to secondary polytopes of finite configurations in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$. We construct an action of the semialgebraic chains of the Fulton--MacPherson operad on the shifted algebra $B_A=\mathfrak g_A[1-d]$ when $|A|\leq3d$. The action recovers the prescribed higher Lie operations on fundamental chains. The construction is obtained from a general extension theorem for weighted shifted $L_\infty$-algebras, using reflection to control relative cohomology obstructions. For $|A|\leq3d-1$, the resulting reflection-compatible integration actions are homotopic relative to their shifted Lie structure. We also give an abstract enhancement without a cardinality bound, direct formulas for circuits, and explicit operations for convex pentagons and hexagons.

papers.title: Deleted square of a cone over a graph
papers.abstract: The deleted square of a topological space is a subspace of the Cartesian product of this space with itself, obtained by removing the diagonal. Conjecturally, the deleted square of a cone over a graph has the homotopy type of a wedge sum of spheres of dimensions at most 3. We propose a geometric construction that is a key motivation for the conjecture and provides a major step towards its proof, while yielding direct results on deleted squares of certain families of graphs.

papers.title: Explicit covers and rigid obstructions for simplicial complexity: from spheres to surfaces
papers.abstract:
The strict simplicial complexity $SC_{\rm strict}(K)$, Gonz\'alez's simplicial complexity at subdivision level zero, is one less than the least number of contiguity domains covering the ordered product $K\times K$. We bound it from both sides. For upper bounds, every product of two vertex stars is a domain, which gives $SC_{\rm strict}(K)\le\rho(K)-1$ for an exactly computable set-cover number $\rho(K)$; the bound is sharp on every even-dimensional simplex boundary. A GPU annealer that evolves whole systems of contiguity chains finds three-domain covers of $\partial\Delta^3,\dots,\partial\Delta^7$ and of the cube boundary. Seeded by star covers, it descends from $24$ to $5$ domains on the icosahedron boundary, and an exact SAT completion of its stalled state gives $SC_{\rm strict}\le3$ there. For lower bounds, a subcomplex of $K\times K$ is rigid if its two projections are joined by no contiguity chain of any length; $k$ domains can cover $K\times K$ only if $k$ classes of facets avoid every rigid subcomplex, a finite SAT problem. Rigid subcomplexes arise from hollow triangles over essential empty triangles and, on complexes without dominated vertices, from the graph of every order-preserving simplicial self-map other than the identity. The resultingchain-length-free bounds give $SC_{\rm strict}(\partial\Delta^{n+1})=2>1=TC(S^n)$ for $n=3,5,7,9$, $SC_{\rm strict}=2>1$ for the five-vertex M\"obius band, $SC_{\rm strict}\ge3>2$ for the seven-vertex torus, and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le5$ and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le6$ for two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$. They also sort the annealer's stalls: on these two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$, the Klein bottle and $\partial\Delta^4$, almost every uncovered
  facet closes a rigid subcomplex in every domain, while the icosahedron stall was a search failure.

papers.title: Face posets, local weight matroids and Betti numbers of torus actions
papers.abstract: Let a compact torus act on a closed manifold $X$ with isolated fixed points. The face poset $S(X)$ of the action is covered by the lattices of flats of the linear matroids of tangent weights at the fixed points. We study how much of the cohomology of $X$ these combinatorial data see. Local equivariant cohomology. The group $H^*_T(X, X\setminus pt)$, embedded in $H^*_T(pt)$ by restriction, is the principal ideal generated by the product of the tangent weights. It determines the weights up to scalars, with multiplicities, and hence the local lattice $S(X)_{\geq pt}$. Local matroids do not suffice. Two connected regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties in $\mathrm{Fl}(\mathbb{C}^5)$, with torus actions of complexity one, have isomorphic weight matroids at all fixed points, and hence the same Chow rings, Orlik–Solomon algebras and Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials there, but different Betti numbers. The face poset determines the Betti numbers of every regular semisimple Hessenberg variety of type A, full or partial, and of the isospectral manifolds of Ayzenberg and Buchstaber. The reason is rigidity: the cluster-permutohedron $\mathrm{Cl}_\Gamma$ determines the graph $\Gamma$, by an elementary argument that recovers the vertices of $\Gamma$ from stars of edges. Simply-laced types. The same holds for regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties of types A, D and E: the face poset determines the Weyl group together with the lines spanned by the roots of the Hessenberg ideal, up to isometry. A formula. The Poincaré polynomial is a sum over the face poset, $P_X(q)=\sum_{\sigma\in S(X)}(q-1)^{\mathrm{rk}\,\sigma}e_\sigma(q)$, in which $e_\sigma$ is a sum of Tutte polynomials of the matroids of weights that are negative on a generic circle. For toric manifolds this is the $h$-vector formula.

papers.title: Graded Monoidal Categories and Internalization
papers.abstract: In stable homotopy theory, there are a variety of ways to construct a point-set level smash product of spectra, each with its own advantages and limitations. These constructions often involve internalizing some graded external product. In this paper, we aim to formalize this process through a general categorical framework, providing a common language for these constructions. We propose a general theory for internalizing a graded monoidal product, investigate its 2-categorical properties, and use this framework to recover both Day convolution and the smash product of $S$-modules.

papers.title: The pentagonal tensor and the fourth obstruction to formality
papers.abstract: Let \(A\) be a connected graded commutative differential graded algebra over \(\mathbb Q\) whose cohomology is a finite-dimensional Poincar\'e duality algebra of formal dimension \(N\ge2\). Assuming that its Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes, we prove that the normalized pentagonal tensor of Nagy and Nordstr\"om, in [preprint (2021), arXiv:2105.13660], vanishes if and only if the fourth Harrison obstruction vanishes after eliminating the third operation. This gives a fourth-order counterpart to the third-order comparison of Fiorenza and L\^e, in [Ann. Sc. Norm. Super. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5), published online 7 March 2025], and answers the vanishing question in L\^e's proposed comparison, in [preprint (2026), arXiv:2603.01219], under the hypothesis that the Bianchi-Massey tensor vanishes. The result applies to closed, connected, oriented manifolds with no upper dimension bound. We also extend Zhou's sphere-bundle formality criterion in [Algebr. Geom. Topol. 25 (2025), pp. 2297--2315] to two-stage oriented sphere bundles with positive odd fibre dimensions over a closed, connected, oriented, rationally formal base, provided that the second Euler class is pulled back from the original base. Their total spaces are rationally formal precisely when the Bianchi-Massey and normalized pentagonal tensors vanish. Our method develops the model-based strategy in Zhou's proof within a commutative bar-cobar framework, providing a starting point for constructing higher tensors and comparing them with higher-order formality obstructions.

papers.title: A $p$-adic de Rham complex
papers.abstract: This is the second in a sequence of three articles exploring the relationship between commutative algebras and $E_\infty$-algebras in characteristic $p$ and mixed characteristic. Given a topological space $X,$ we construct, in a manner analogous to Sullivan's $A_{PL}$-functor, a strictly commutative algebra over $\padic$ which we call the de Rham forms on $X$. We show this complex computes the singular cohomology ring of $X$. We prove that it is quasi-isomorphic as an $E_\infty$-algebra to the Berthelot-Ogus-Deligne \emph{d\'ecalage} of the singular cochains complex with respect to the $p$-adic filtration. We show that one can extract concrete invariants from our model, including Massey products which live in the torsion part of the cohomology. We show that if $X$ is formal then, except at possibly finitely many primes, the $p$-adic de Rham forms on $X$ are also formal. We conclude by showing that the $p$-adic de Rham forms provide, in a certain sense, the "best functorial strictly commutative approximation" to the singular cochains complex.

papers.title: A counterexample to a folklore conjecture on Gelfand pairs
papers.abstract: We construct a connected symmetric pair over $\Q_5$ for which every irreducible unramified principal series has at most one invariant linear form, whereas an explicit irreducible admissible representation has exactly two. The ambient group is the subgroup of $\GL_2\times\GL_2$ defined by $\det(g_1)\det(g_2)=1$, and the symmetric subgroup is a twisted diagonal copy of $\SL_2$. The construction uses the two constituents of the restriction to $\SL_2(\Q_5)$ of a quadratic principal series of $\GL_2(\Q_5)$. It gives a counterexample to the formulation of a folklore conjecture on Gelfand pairs recorded by Aizenbud and Sayag in terms of generic unramified principal series.

papers.title: A counterexample to local Tor-length bounds
papers.abstract: We exhibit complete-intersection ideals generated by regular sequences of lengths three and four in a four-dimensional regular local ring. Their common quotient has length eight, and their Tor modules have lengths (8,22,22,8), with all higher Tor modules zero. Thus both the proposed binomial lower bound in degree one and the proposed total-length bound fail. The calculation uses a graded Koszul complex on a sixteen-dimensional algebra. The local-ring statement and the Tor-length table are verified in Lean.

papers.title: A counterexample to rank log-concavity of Bruhat intervals
papers.abstract: We disprove Brenti's conjecture that Bruhat intervals in Weyl groups are rank log-concave by constructing an explicit counterexample in a finite symmetric group.

papers.title: A fake quadric that is not a bidisk quotient
papers.abstract: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a construction of a fake quadric $S$ that is a $32$-fold branched cover of $\mathbf{CP}^1\times\mathbf{CP}^1$ along nine curves. This configuration is given by four horizontal lines, four vertical lines and the diagonal. We show that $S$ is not aspherical. As a corollary the universal cover of $S$ is not the bidisk $\mathbf{H}\times\mathbf{H}$.

papers.title: A Note on Binary Quadratic Systems and their relation to complexity theory
papers.abstract:
Deciding whether a system of multivariate quadratic equations over $\mathbb F_2$ has a solution is a classical NP-complete problem, and remains so for square systems, with as many equations as variables. The hardness of this problem is one of the cornerstones of nowadays post-quantum cryptography. Let $\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)$ and $\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)$ denote the sets of square quadratic systems in $n$ variables having respectively no solutions and exactly one solution. $\cup_{n\geq 2} \mathrm{MQ}_0(n)$ is a coNP-complete language, while $\cup_{n\geq 2} \mathrm{MQ}_1(n)$ lies in DP. It is known that $\lim_{n\to \infty} |\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)|/|\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|=1$. Here we prove the explicit finite-$n$ bounds \[ |\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|<|\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)| \le \left(1+\frac{1}{2^n-1}\right)|\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|, \]
  More generally, let $Q_d$ be the space of polynomial functions $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n\to\mathbb F_2$ of degree at most $d$, and let $\alpha_k$ count square systems in $(Q_d)^n$ having exactly $k$ solutions. Then \[ \alpha_0<\alpha_1 \le \left(1+\frac{1}{2^n-1}\right)\alpha_0\,, \qquad 2\le d\le n \,. \] The proof combines matroid and coding-theoretic methods. We interpret $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$ as the ground set of the evaluation matroid of $Q_d$, express $\alpha_0$ and $\alpha_1$ through characteristic polynomials, and use a Whitney-type sign-reversing involution to show that the only terms that can push $\alpha_1-\alpha_0$ below $\alpha_1/2^n$ come from the elements of a matroid port. These are identified with minimal-support words of the Reed--Muller code $\mathrm{RM}(n-d-1,n)=\mathrm{RM}(d,n)^\perp$; the required estimate then follows from the MacWilliams identity, the minimum-distance bound $2^{d+1}$, and the even-weight structure of the code.

papers.title: A Peterson program for general Schubert varieties and mirror symmetry
papers.abstract: We initiate a `Peterson program' that seeks to extend Dale Peterson's theory for the quantum cohomology of flag varieties to arbitrary Schubert varieties, and that incorporates a mirror-symmetric approach. In this first paper we introduce a generalisation of the (localised) Peterson variety associated to an arbitrary Schubert variety $\check X_{w,P}$ inside a partial flag variety $\check G/\check P$. This generalisation is possibly a non-reduced affine scheme that lies in the Langlands dual full flag variety $G/B$. Additionally, we construct a Lie-theoretic `superpotential' associated to $\check X_{w,P}$, generalising earlier ones for the flag varieties $\check G/\check P$ from [Rie08], and we show that its relative critical point locus recovers the generalised Peterson variety. We make the key conjecture that for smooth Fano Schubert varieties the coordinate ring of the generalised Peterson variety recovers the quantum cohomology ring of $\check X_{w,P}$ localised at the quantum parameters. For smooth Fano Schubert varieties $X_{w,B}$ in $\check G/\check B$ we furthermore map our generalised Peterson variety to the cotangent bundle $\mathcal T^*(T)$ of the maximal torus $T$ of $G$ and construct a partial compactification that we conjecture models the full quantum cohomology ring of $\check X_{w,B}$, in analogy with the Givental-Kim presentation of $QH^*(\check G/\check B)$ via the degenerate leaf of the Kostant Toda lattice of $\check G$. These conjectures are verified for all smooth Schubert divisors in the complete type $A$ flag variety, and we show that our superpotential agrees with that introduced for Grassmannian Schubert varieties by Rietsch and Williams, after a suitable isomorphism of the domains.

papers.title: A PROOF OF LINCKELMANN’S CONJECTURE ON OUTER DERIVATIONS OF BLOCKS
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a block of a finite group algebra over a field of positive characteristic. We prove that if $B$ has positive defect, then $HH^1(B) \neq 0$, as conjectured by Linckelmann. In fact, the degree-one Batalin–Vilkovisky operator $HH^1(B) \rightarrow Z(B)$ is nonzero. A minimal- counterexample argument reduces the proof to a question about fusion in quasisimple groups. We handle the remaining small defect groups using a local criterion involving the projective centre of a central quotient.

papers.title: A proposed proof of Cazenave's Conjecture 6(iii)
papers.abstract: We give a proposed proof of Cazenave's Conjecture 6(iii). For every finite simple connected graph on at least two vertices, the square of the largest Laplacian eigenvalue is at least four times the second-largest adjacency eigenvalue plus eight. The argument treats graphs of maximum degree three using exact Rayleigh quotients for small subgraphs and bounds on the adjacency eigenvalues.

papers.title: A Syntactic Approach to Ulmer's Bialgebras
papers.abstract:
Ulmer proposed to view a bialgebraic structure on an object $x$ as a structure map $f\colon Fx\to Gx$ satisfying an equation $\alpha_{(x,f)} = \beta_{(x,f)}$ of natural transformations. This perspective is powerful enough to account for many algebraic and coalgebraic structures, such as varieties of universal algebra, categories of algebras over a PROP, an operad or a monad. We develop Ulmer's bialgebras within a $2$-categorical setting with PIE limits, where structure maps are abstracted by inserters and their equations by equifiers. A syntax of signatures, theories and models is then used to produce these bialgebraic structures. The syntax of the commutative diagrams defining Hopf algebras can be used, as is, to define the $0$-cell of Hopf algebras within any symmetric pseudomonoid in a $2$-category with PIE limits.
  In this setting, we show that lax morphisms of models induce morphisms between the objects of algebras, extending the classical result lifting a lax monoidal functor to a functor between the categories of internal monoids. Since the construction of the object of bialgebras is expressed entirely in terms of PIE limits, we show that Kan extensions, accessibility, local presentability, orthogonal factorization systems, regularity, and Barr-exactness lift along the construction under suitable assumptions. A bi-dense class of objects allows us to transfer monadicity and local presentability results to formal settings. Finally, we construct a bi-dense class of $\V$-categories with at most three objects, where $\V$ is any monoidal category with an absorbing initial object.

papers.title: Algebraic Comparison of Torus Boundary States and an Obstruction to Completion
papers.abstract: Torus boundary states admit both root-of-unity coordinates and formal-series descriptions, but identifying finite states need not identify their completions. We construct an injective algebraic comparison between compatible Newton interpolation and Hopf-pairing data and the coefficient models of Gukov--Manolescu and Guicardi--Jagadale. The common domain is \(\mathbb Z[A,A^{-1}][v]\), with three copies indexed by the nonzero mod-two residues of half-integral exponent lattices. A chosen filling functional takes value one on its normalized reference state and zero on an independent state. The domain exhausts the finite states generated from the reference state by the specified spectral coordinate over the common coefficient ring. We then impose uniform formal convergence together with discrete root coordinates on the first model and specified uniform Laurent-series topologies on the other two. A cyclotomic interpolation sequence converges to zero in the first model and to the reference state in the other two. Every coordinate projection of the resulting closed relation is therefore noninjective. The obstruction persists in extensions retaining these topologies and the scalar multiples of the reference state. The same sequence produces a zero-framed trefoil limit, whose relation to a negative-definite plumbing retains an explicitly computed framing scalar in the target coefficient field.

papers.title: An exponential lower bound on the exact stabilizer rank
papers.abstract: For the single-qubit state $|T\rangle = (|0\rangle + e^{i\pi/4}|1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$, we prove that the minimum number of stabilizer states in an exact linear decomposition of $|T\rangle^{\otimes n}$ grows exponentially in $n$. The proof combines the tripartite stabilizer normal form with a spectral point obtained from OpenAI's preprint on Euclidean geometry in the asymptotic spectrum of tensors.

papers.title: Approximate Coloring Is a Promise CSP
papers.abstract: The contribution contains: 1. A direct reduction from 3-SAT to approximate coloring without using the PCP theorem. For each fixed n ≥ 3, the task is to find an n-coloring of a graph promised to be 3-colorable. 2. A new notion of minion homomorphism that explains this reduction. The polymorphism minions of 3-SAT and approximate coloring admit such maps in both directions. Soundness follows from an extension of the Barto–Kozik baby PCP theorem. 3. A combination of existing and new reductions that prove a dichotomy for promise CSPs on pairs of finite digraphs without sources or sinks. 4. An unconditional dichotomy for finite Boolean promise CSPs whose polymorphisms are unate. The tractable cases admit block-symmetric polymorphisms on two arbitrarily large blocks. The hardness proof uses an injective extension of the new baby PCP theorem. 5. NP-hardness for seven families of promise CSPs studied in the literature.

papers.title: Birational $\mathbb P^2$-bundle structures and toric 2-Fano manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a general birational program toward the classification of toric 2-Fano manifolds through the investigation of the minimal projective bundle dimension \(m(X) \in \{1,\dots,\dim(X)\}\) introduced in our previous work. This invariant captures the minimal degree of a dominating family of rational curves on \(X\) and admits a natural combinatorial interpretation in terms of centered primitive collections. We establish a general obstruction to being 2-Fano in terms of the existence of projective bundle structures and prove a birational reduction theorem for toric Fano manifolds with \(m(X)=2\). This allows us to show that the only toric 2-Fano manifold \(X\) with \(m(X) = 2\) is \(X\cong \mathbb{P}^2\). We also investigate how this strategy might extend to \(m\ge3\).

papers.title: Breaking the Linear-Ansatz Barrier for the Sum-of-Square-Roots Problem: r(n, k) = O(n^{-2k + 1/2}) for All k >= 2, Sharp k = 2 Separation Bounds, and Lean 4 Formalization
papers.abstract: We prove that for every integer k >= 2, the minimal non-zero separation r(n, k) between two sums of k square roots of integers bounded by n satisfies r(n, k) = O(n^{-2k + 1/2}), improving the 20-year-old constructive upper bound O(n^{-2k + 3/2}) of Qian and Wang (Information Processing Letters, 2006) by a full factor of n for all k >= 2 and matching the birthday-paradox heuristic exponent. We prove that linear radicands hit an insurmountable Vandermonde wall at O(n^{-2k + 3/2}) and bypass it via an even-symmetric quadratic radical ansatz with a single conjugate pair, a universal 3-torsion derivative identity psi_3'(0) = 196608 a delta_Q^10 n_1 c_0^5 != 0, universal R -> infinity nodal scaling limits, Mazur's Torsion Theorem, and Kronecker density. We also provide explicit polynomial families for k = 2, 3, 4, sharp effective lower bounds for k = 2 (r(n, 2) >= 1/(4 n^3 sqrt(n)) for all n >= 1, 4096x sharper than BFMS, and exact asymptotic constant 8/27), an analysis of the 7-moment Diophantine barrier for k = 3 (85.4M candidates tested), and a complete Lean 4.36.0 formalization of our explicit k = 2 and k = 3 theorems (1,222 library lines, zero sorry, zero native_decide, standard axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]).

papers.title: Butson towers and high-rank Hadamard matrices
papers.abstract: We construct eighteen new real Hadamard matrices of ranks 7572, 17668, 22716, 32812, 42908, 58052, 73196, 78244, 93388, 98436, 108532, 128724, 153964, 229684, 295308, 386172, 4772884 and 13001124, and six new infinite families. The constructions preserve orthogonality and ensure that every final entry is 1 or -1. Explicit recipes and reproducible formal proofs establish every listed rank and every member of the six families.

papers.title: Characterizations of E-finite algebras and conjectures on brick-finiteness
papers.abstract: A finite-dimensional algebra over a field is called E-finite if every difference of classes of finitely generated projective modules lies in a two-term silting cone. Over an arbitrary field, we prove that an algebra is E-finite if and only if any two nonzero finite-dimensional modules with the same dimension vector admit a nonzero homomorphism in each direction. Using this criterion, we show that E-finiteness is also equivalent to finiteness of every semibrick, functorial finiteness of every wide subcategory of finite-dimensional modules, finiteness of the number of isomorphism classes of finite-dimensional bricks of each endolength, and nonexistence of generic bricks, along with further conditions on torsion classes, universal localizations, and moduli spaces. Consequently, several open problems become equivalent for each algebra, each asking whether every E-finite algebra is brick-finite; among them are Demonet's lattice point conjecture, the finite semibrick conjecture, the endolength form of the second brick-Brauer--Thrall conjecture and Pfeifer's stable variant, Mousavand and Paquette's generic brick conjecture, and the wide subcategory question of Angeleri H\"ugel and Sentieri. Finally, we prove that every E-finite algebra with at most two nonisomorphic simple modules is brick-finite over any field.

papers.title: Cohomology of pseudo-reductive groups over local function fields
papers.abstract: We give a pairing which describes the first Galois cohomology of a pseudo-reductive group $G$ over a local function field $K$ as the Pontryagin dual of the group $\Ext^1(G, \Gm)$ of translation-invariant line bundles on $G$. In order to accomplish this, we endow the Picard group of a scheme $X$ over a (Hausdorff) topological field with a topology, and prove that this topology enjoys favorable properties under certain mild conditions on $X$ and on the field.

papers.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
papers.abstract: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.

papers.title: Connectedness Principle in the Complex Analytic Setting
papers.abstract: We show that if $(X,B)$ is a normal compact K\"ahler pair and $f:X\to Z$ is a proper morphism with connected fibers to a normal compact K\"ahler variety $Z$ such that $(-K_X+B)$ is nef over $Z$, then $\mathrm{Nklt}(X,B)\cap f^{-1}(z)$ has at most two connected components for every $z\in Z$. More generally, we prove the result for generalized pairs whose nef part is allowed to be transcendental. Moreover, we record that the same result holds for projective morphism between analytic varieties (possibly non-compact).

papers.title: Counting contingency tables, Kostka numbers, and Littlewood--Richardson coefficients with unary inputs is #P-complete
papers.abstract: We prove that counting contingency tables with prescribed unary margins is $\#P$-complete under polynomial-time Turing reductions for both cases of tables with nonnegative integer entries and entries in $\{0,1\}$. This proves a Conjecture of Pak and Panova. The methods involve modular arithmetic by repeating margins $p$-times and relating to the SETPARTITION problem. The congruences are proven using symmetric function techniques. We also realize each nonnegative table count as a single rectangular Kostka number, and then as a Littlewood--Richardson coefficient with a rectangular factor. Both coefficient problems are therefore $\#$P-complete for partitions given in unary making Kostka and Littlewood-Richardson coefficients strongly $\#$P-complete. For permutations in one-line notation, computing a Schubert structure constant is consequently $\#$P-hard even when all three permutations are Grassmannian with a common descent.

papers.title: Decomposition algorithms for rational curves on real classical groups
papers.abstract:
This paper is devoted to an algorithmic investigation of the decomposition problem for rational curves on real classical groups. The main contributions are:
  (1) We present two Maple-implemented algorithms for decomposing rational curves on real classical groups. The first algorithm decomposes a curve with multiple poles into a unique product of curves with single poles. For rational curves on (indefinite) orthogonal groups, the second algorithm further decomposes single-pole curves into products of low-degree curves. The former only involves linear equations, whereas the latter requires solving both linear and quadratic equations.
  (2) We compare the decomposition of the same curve with respect to different ambient groups. Through this comparison, we provide an interpretation of the "multiplication trick" for motion polynomials within our framework. Moreover, we demonstrate that our second algorithm aligns with this trick.
  (3) We prove that the solvability of linear equations in the second algorithm is preserved under the extension of the ambient group.
  For illustration, we provide comprehensive computational examples.

papers.title: Differential transcendence of cubic and quartic polynomial series
papers.abstract: We prove that the characteristic generating function of the values of any integer-valued quartic polynomial with positive leading coefficient satisfies no algebraic differential equation, even after restricting its nonnegative integer inputs to a nonempty union of residue classes. In particular, this proves the fourth-power case of the conjecture of Chowla and Chowla. The proof extends Helminen's theorem for the cubic series $\sum_{n\ge0}q^{n^3}$. We give a self-contained exposition of his argument and establish the additional analytic estimates required for quartics. Exact Fourier decompositions separate exponential contributions whose arithmetic labels lead to an invertible Vandermonde matrix.

papers.title: Diophantine definitions of $\mathbb{Z}$ in totally real fields from rank-one elliptic curves
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a totally real number field, let $E\colon y^2=x^3-Ax$ be one of four explicit elliptic curves over a real quadratic field $F\not\subseteq K$, and put $L=KF$. We prove that if $E(L)$ has rank one and torsion in $E[2]$, and $2E(L)\subseteq E(F)$, then $\mathbb{Z}$ is Diophantine in $K$, with $25$ unknowns, so Hilbert's tenth problem over $K$ has a negative answer. For a suitable curve these conditions hold for every layer of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, for infinitely many real quadratic fields and for some further fields of degree at most $8$. The construction is Z.-W. Sun's, from his proofs for $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$, $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt3)$ and $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt6)$, except that our predicate excluding poles of odd order uses the congruent-number twists of our earlier proof for $\mathbb{Q}$. Its main step is a height bound on a $q$-adic tube of a quaternionic Shimura curve. We prove it over every totally real field by Sun's method, with a scalar cochain over $K$, a comparison with Shimura curves over $K$ in every degree and, when $\sqrt3\in K$, a second tube prime.

papers.title: Division by Two Cycles in Binary and Explicit Representations
papers.abstract: Let \(A\) be a permutation with two cycles and \(B\) a target permutation. We ask whether \(B\) is isomorphic to the synchronous product \(AX\) for some quotient \(X\), how to construct one, and how many quotients there are up to isomorphism. Suppose the cycle lengths in \(A\) are \(2\) and an odd \(b>1\). If the input lists cycle lengths and multiplicities in binary, deciding existence is NP-complete and counting quotient classes is \(\#\mathsf P\)-complete under parsimonious polynomial-time reductions. Given the successor of each state, we can count the classes and construct one quotient whenever it exists, both in polynomial time. For arbitrary cycle lengths \(a,b\) of \(A\), put \(g=\gcd(a,b)\). In either representation we construct, in deterministic polynomial time, a new target and a divisor with cycle lengths \(gd,g(d+1)\), \(d\ge2\). The resulting bijection on quotient classes is computable in polynomial time in both directions. For each fixed \(g\), varying \(d\) gives the same two completeness results for binary lists. With \(d=2\) fixed and \(g\) varying, one binary quotient can be found in polynomial time whenever it exists. Deciding whether there are at least two classes is polynomial-time Turing equivalent to integer factorisation. For two arbitrary divisor lengths, division from successor tables is decidable in polynomial time if and only if Boolean satisfiability on \(m\)-bit formulas is decidable in deterministic time \(m^{O(\log\log m)}\). We can count quotient classes in polynomial time if and only if satisfying assignments can be counted within that time bound. Both equivalences and the bijection extend to explicit targets with transient states.

papers.title: Enhanced Helgason-Johnson bounds for classical groups of type $B$
papers.abstract: This paper improves the Helgason-Johnson bound in 1969 for non-Hermitian real classical groups of type $B$.

papers.title: Euclidean Tensor Prices and Sharp Multiquadratic Composition Bounds
papers.abstract: Conditional on two recent results, the Euclidean price theorem announced by OpenAI on 24 November 2026 and Khoruzhii's integral crossing lemma, we determine the exponent of the sum-of-squares composition problem for every fixed number of factors. Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two, a product of $k$ sums of squares, the $i$-th in $\lceil n^{\beta_i}\rceil$ variables, is a sum of $n^{\|\beta\|_2+o(1)}$ squares of multilinear forms, and of no fewer; for $k$ blocks of equal size the exponent is $\sqrt k$. The same exponent holds for the partial-transpose rank of the identity matrix over every field, and for the border versions of both quantities. The lower bound comes from the price theorem and holds at finite sizes with explicit constants; the upper bound composes crossing decompositions recursively. Combined with an argument of Liu, the price theorem also shows that noncommutative circuits for the permanent and the determinant of order $N$ have size at least $2^{N/2-O(\sqrt{N\log N})}$ over every field, even in the border model. We have not verified the proof of the price theorem, on which every lower bound here depends.

papers.title: Euler Transport for the Quadratic Dedekind Zeta Function: a Verified Reduction of the Quadratic Factorisation on Prove2Me
papers.abstract: We report a machine-verified reduction of the quadratic factorisation milestone of the Class Number Formula mission on the Prove2Me platform: for a quadratic number field K with discriminant d and Kronecker character chi, the identity zeta_K(s) = zeta(s) L(s, chi) for Re(s) > 1 together with the residue identity lim_{s->1+} (s-1) zeta_K(s) = L(1, chi) is reduced, with zero loss of constant, to three open lemmas: the Euler-factor transport itself, the nontriviality chi != 1, and an analytic residue transport. The reduction was found by the wormhole method (cross-domain transport along an explicit correspondence) and is packaged for completion by the self-contained-file method measured on the platform's most prolific solver. The parent theorem auto-resolves once the three leaves are proved, and the leaves feed both cases of Dirichlet's class number formula.

papers.title: Eventual interlacing of large-block set-partition polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $P_n(t)$ count set partitions of $[n]$ by the number of blocks of size at least four. For all sufficiently large $n$, its $\lfloor n/4\rfloor$ zeros are simple and negative, and $P_n$ interlaces $P_{n+j}$ strictly in the prescribed direction for $1\le j\le4$. The proof matches absolute zero counts at a reciprocal-polynomial limit and an Airy limit, using uniform saddle estimates between them. The global angular minimum on a bounded range of radii is certified with outward-rounded interval arithmetic. We give the limiting empirical zero distribution, fixed-rank asymptotics and adjacent-row displacement at the Airy edge, and effective bounds at both ends. Integer and interval computations certify every nonconstant row through $2004$. We also prove a coefficient-order inequality valid for every block-size threshold.

papers.title: Exact sequences of regular LF-spaces
papers.abstract: We show that the category of regular LF-spaces has all kernels but, unlike the category of regular LB-spaces, does not have all cokernels. Its topological exact structure, maximal exact structure and maximal deflation-exact structure form a strictly increasing chain of proper subclasses of the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs. To the best of the authors' knowledge, regular LF-spaces in particular provide the first natural example of a category that has all kernels but is not preabelian and whose maximal deflation-exact structure is neither two-sided exact nor equal to the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs.

papers.title: Explicit lattice packings
papers.abstract: We give explicit lattices in large dimension $n$ with packing density at least $2^{-1.2463n}$. The best previous explicit lattices reached $2^{-1.3889n}$. A simpler version of the construction reaches $2^{-1.3n}$, and a basis can be computed in time polynomial in $n$. We build the lattices from the Leech lattice, a Ramanujan graph and algebraic-geometry codes. We also explain what would be needed to push the same construction past the Minkowski-Hlawka bound $2^{-n}$.

papers.title: Finite attainment in Révész's cosine extremal problem
papers.abstract: Among nonnegative continuous cosine series with constant term $1$, first coefficient $a$, and nonnegative higher coefficients, consider the infimum of the value at zero. A trigonometric polynomial attains this infimum exactly when $|a|\leq 4/3$. Outside this interval every admissible polynomial can be improved by introducing one higher frequency, chosen by simultaneous approximation at its zeros. This answers the finite-degree question of Révész, including the case $a=1.85$. As a consequence, every admissible polynomial has objective strictly above Landau's infimum $V$. An explicit sum of two squared moduli of degree $126$ gives $V<34.488157$.

papers.title: Formally Verified Asymptotic Optimality of Parallel Find-Any Search and Machine-Checked Benchmark Improvements in Lean 4
papers.abstract: A general finite-n query lower bound and an exact asymptotic optimality theorem are proved in Lean 4.35.0 for parallel GroverFindAny under the frozen specifications of DeepMind's formal-quantum-computation benchmark suite (arXiv:2611.09822v3). While the restricted single-checkpoint infimum rho_* = 1/2 + 1/pi was previously established by Fang and Heunen (2026), it is proved here that inf{R in R : Feasible(m,k,R)} = 1/2 + 1/pi across all OracleDynamicCircuit programs--permitting arbitrary finite workspace, adaptive intermediate measurements, and nested qWhile loops under uniform k-subset averaging, probability-one success, and expected parallel rounds--on all 121 dyadic grid cells. Two supplementary verified constructions are presented: a 5/16-module rewrite by which ArcsinK25ConstCost is reduced from 369,800 to 366,200 (3,662 T x 100 Q, TOFF=0, -0.9735%, with exact compiled counts and a 100-qubit non-vacuity witness), and single-cell (1024, 512) GroverFindAll bounds lowered by 0.038% (sign-only walk) and 0.946% (to 26,768,771,052/10^12 via 14 Kraus filters with restarts, proved uniformly for all n >= 80,000 above the inherited cutoff, exact fallback below); partial THCFactorization foundations are documented in Appendix B. All new derivations, formalizations, audits, and prose were produced purely by AI systems under human supervision; formal claims are machine-checked in Lean 4.35.0 against frozen libraries using standard axioms only, with the flagship FindAny theorems also accepted by two third-party kernels (nanoda, con-ron).

papers.title: Fractional moments of the sharp Möbius divisor sum on integers and reflected primes
papers.abstract: Let $M_R(n)=\sum_{d\mid n,\,d\le R}\mu(d)$ and $Y=\min(R,X/R)$. We determine the exponent of $\log Y$ in every absolute moment of order $0<s\le2$ as $Y\to\infty$. Up to the transition $s_*=2\log(1/\log 2)/\log 2$ the exponent is the exponent for the support of $M_R$. Strictly below the transition the mean has the order of that support, including its factor $(\log\log Y)^{-3/2}$. Above it the exponent is $2^{s/2}-1-s/2$. The same laws hold on $n=N-p$ for an individual even $N$ with fixed radical, at either $R=Y$ or $R=N/Y$ and $Y\le N^{1/2-\epsilon}$. With probability proportional to $M_R(n)^2$, the small-prime-factor count and $\log|M_R(n)|$ have the same normalized Gaussian fluctuation for $Y\le N^{1/4-\epsilon}$. The arguments use the Fourier transform of a signed divisor sum, localized divisor counts, and a lower sieve on the prime variable.

papers.title: Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings, with applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings and give applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers. We realize rational double points of ADE over $W(k)$ as invariant subrings $A^G$, where $A$ is a ramified two-dimensional complete regular local ring and $G$ is a finite linearly reductive subgroup scheme of $\mathrm{SL}_{2,W(k)}$. We also prove a general theorem on the existence of Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings: if a flat affine group scheme $G$ over $W(k)$ admits a functorial Reynolds operator and a relative Frobenius lift, then any formal power series ring equipped with a linear action of $G$ admits a Frobenius lift that restricts to a Frobenius lift on the invariant subring. Building on these results, we construct perfectoid towers arising from rational double points in mixed characteristic. We identify their tilts with the perfect towers arising from rational double points in positive characteristic of the same ADE type.

papers.title: Gaussian Continued Fractions of the Non-Real Zeros of the Goodspeed Function
papers.abstract: We investigate Gaussian continued fractions of the phase coordinates associated with the non-real zeros of the Goodspeed function \[ G(z)=\frac{1}{\pi^2} \left( \sin^2(\pi z)+ \sin^2\left(\pi\frac{\Gamma(z)+1}{z}\right) \right). \] An exact logarithmic correction identifies the first Gaussian continued-fraction digit at sufficiently high zeros and yields exponential bounds for the next digit. For a canonical sequence of non-real zeros accumulating at the origin, we establish four distinct asymptotic laws for the continued-fraction digits. One of these integer-valued digit sequences determines the first two nontrivial coefficients of the underlying holomorphic germ. We further prove that the subsequent Gaussian digit eventually belongs to an explicitly determined alphabet of 31 Gaussian integers, and calculate the limiting frequency of every state. The frequency law follows from the asymptotic geometry of the zero sequence and equidistribution of a fractional-power phase. These results provide a continued-fraction and symbolic description of a distinguished non-real zero family, independently of conjectures concerning the global classification of Goodspeed zeros.

papers.title: Genus one mirror symmetry and surfaces with trivial first Chern class
papers.abstract:
The main goal of this paper is to study the extension of genus-one BCOV type mirror symmetry for smooth projective varieties with vanishing $c_1(X)$. We show that the naive generalization of the expectation that one can encode genus one Gromov-Witten invariants in the BCOV invariant of the mirror family cannot hold in this setup. We show this by completing the study of these invariants for surfaces. Progress had been made recently by Oberdieck's proof of the Klemm-Mari\~no conjecture for Enriques surfaces, which can be combined with computations of equivariant analytic torsion by Yoshikawa. We also perform the analogous study for bielliptic surfaces.
  Both of these cases present a sign issue not present in the known trivial canonical bundle cases, which we show implies that the mirror symmetry predictions cannot hold for varieties with torsion canonical bundle, even up to sign.

papers.title: Gerbe-corrected stringy E-functions
papers.abstract: We define an invariant of $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein complex varieties with at worst log-terminal singularities equipped with a rational Brauer class $\alpha$ that generalizes existing versions of the $\alpha$-corrected stringy $E$-polynomial, which are defined only for quotients of quasi-projective varieties by finite groups. Using recent results from $p$-adic integration, this new invariant can be shown to behave well for degenerate dual abelian fibrations and to agree with the intersection or BPS $E$-polynomial for certain moduli problems.

papers.title: Hall deficiency one at the distinct-multiples threshold
papers.abstract: In the divisibility matching of Erdős and Pomerance, consider the last interval too short to admit distinct multiples of 1 through n. We show that every set violating Hall's condition in this interval has deficiency exactly one. The observation follows from deleting a single right vertex at the first feasible threshold. Matching computations verify it for n from 1 through 10,000, and a census of all subsets gives the number of violations for n from 1 through 22.

papers.title: Heegaard realizations of unified WRT invariants and radial comparisons with $\widehat Z$: The Poincaré sphere and completion obstructions
papers.abstract: We compare Heegaard realizations of the Witten--Reshetikhin--Turaev (WRT) invariant, Habiro's unified invariant, and homological-block \(\widehat Z\) series, keeping their distinct coefficient and convergence domains. For the Poincar\'e sphere, a genus-two gluing adapted to an open-book page computes the canonical extended Reshetikhin--Turaev scalar at every root order \(k\ge2\). An explicit lift to a joint cyclotomic and power-series completion then recovers the oriented block, including its exceptional additive term. For Heegaard gluings with unimodular meridian-to-longitude block, finite Gram-matrix sewing and capping realize Habiro's known unified invariant in arbitrary genus. Composing this realization with Murakami's theorem gives a radial comparison on its stated class of negative-definite unimodular plumbings satisfying its leaf condition. Completion and nonuniqueness obstructions explain why root values alone do not determine a disk series; in particular, the matched-order Bailey polynomials for \(\Sigma(2,3,7)\) do not form the required compatible cyclotomic sequence. A separate rank-one calculation identifies the refined scalar vacuum and its shifted refinement parameter.

papers.title: Higher-Dimensional Automata in Geometric Logic
papers.abstract: What does the topos of a higher-dimensional automaton know about its infinite behaviour that its language does not? We write partial HDAs with an infinite run as models of a geometric theory over an intuitionistic metatheory with no choice. The topos of a machine is that of sheaves on its prefixes. The label word of a prefix records the shape and acceptance bit of each cell with the ipomset of each step. Under unique choice these words give a geometric morphism to the label topos of sheaves on label words, which thus records the shapes and acceptance bits that the B\"uchi language forgets. Machines sharing their B\"uchi language and their frames can differ over the label topos. The bouquet of two squares shares its frame and its B\"uchi language with the interleaved square; each accepted run of either reads the two events in parallel forever. Only the interleaved square has runs through cells of shape a, and the geometric sequent excluding such runs separates the two over the label topos. Over alphabets with decidable equality, finite rigid machines are unambiguous exactly when their label maps are inclusions of locales, and their equivalence over the label topos is decided whenever either is unambiguous. Equivalences of frames over the label topos transport points with their labels, and the invariants of fibres and of the language of points follow from this transport. On finite partial HDAs over alphabets with decidable equality, Muller and B\"uchi acceptance coincide exactly under a weak form of excluded middle.

papers.title: Holomorphy for homogeneous polynomials with ordinary singularities
papers.abstract: We prove a vanishing theorem for twisted Igusa integrals of homogeneous polynomials whose projective hypersurfaces are reduced and have only isolated ordinary multiple points. Under Denef's monodromy exclusion, the integrals on the integer polydisc and its origin residue class vanish outside finitely many places, uniformly in the character. We also compute the integral on every residue class.

papers.title: Interlacing triangles with an alternating bottom row
papers.abstract: We enumerate interlacing triangles whose bottom row begins with an ascent and then alternates. At size eight there are exactly 22,726,530,931,960,444,539,200 such triangles. We give the counts for sizes one through eight and the accompanying table of all bottom-row patterns. At each tested size from two through eight, the two alternating patterns are the only ones attaining the largest count.

papers.title: Invariance of log plurigenera in families of compact K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $(X_t,B_t)$ be a smooth proper family of pairs with K\"ahler fibres, where the boundary has relative simple normal crossings and real coefficients in $[0,1)$. We show that for every $m\ge1$, every section of $mK_{X_t}+\lfloor mB_t\rfloor$ extends locally over the base. In particular, the log plurigenera are locally constant, and for $B_t=0$ we obtain the deformation invariance of the plurigenera $P_m(X_t)$. Since the total space need not be K\"ahler, we run the minimal model program on the central fibre, using the work of Hacon-Wang and Hacon-Xie, and extend its steps over a disc. The obstruction to lifting a jet vanishes along the fixed part determined by the final model, and so it is square-integrable for the weight in the extension theorem of Cao-P\u{a}un. As an application, if the adjoint is pseudoeffective on one fibre, then the pair has a relative good minimal model near each point of the base and a relative canonical model over the whole base.

papers.title: Irreducible trinomials over the binary field: an elliptic-curve criterion and explicit families
papers.abstract: We study irreducible trinomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Using an elliptic curve and reciprocity laws, we prove that, for $k \ge 2$, $X^{(4^k+2)/3}+X+1$ is irreducible if and only if $4^k+3$ is prime and $2$ is a primitive root modulo that prime. By power substitution and linearization, we also assemble explicit infinite families of irreducible trinomials $X^m+X^n+1$ in fourteen distinct reduced exponent classes.

papers.title: Ising spins with Hadamard couplings
papers.abstract: A real Hadamard matrix $H$ of order $N$ defines a system of $2N$ Ising spins, carried by 2 layers of crossed wires, with couplings $H_{jk}/\sqrt N$ between the layers. This is the switching game of Gale and Berlekamp at finite temperature, and having symmetric orthogonal couplings, it is a deterministic instance of the random orthogonal model of Marinari, Parisi and Ritort. The density of states is the real glow of $H$. We show that its law modulo 16 is determined by $N$ and the 2-rank $r$ of $H$, that its moments are universal polynomials in $N$ up to order 14, the first correction being given by the 4-profile of $H$, and that the high-temperature expansion of the free energy is universal to leading order, with a continued paramagnetic entropy which vanishes at $\beta=\sqrt{240}$. At $N=16$ the 5 densities of states form a 1-parameter family, the parameter being the number $2^{14-r}-128$ of crystalline ground states, at $N=20$ they coincide, and at $N=24,28,32$ they form families with 2, 4 and at least 8 parameters.

papers.title: Kov\'acs Vanishing for Excellent Log Canonical Threefolds
papers.abstract: We prove a vanishing theorem of S. Kov\'acs for excellent log canonical threefolds whose closed points have perfect residue fields of sufficiently large characteristic. This vanishing theorem roughly says that LC threefold pairs are not far from being rational pairs (in the sense of Koll\'ar \& Kov\'acs and Schwede \& Takagi) if one includes a correction term. We apply this vanishing to prove a depth relation of Chou and resolution-invariance of cohomologies of ``essential divisors" for isolated log canonical threefolds in large characteristic, extending works of Ishii and Fujino. Using examples constructed by Bernasconi and Cascini-Tanaka, we show that these results fail in low characteristic. Finally, we show Kov\'acs and Alexeev-Hacon's result (in char 0) that ``Irrational centers are LC centers" fails in every positive characteristic.

papers.title: Lifting Cocycles: From Heuristic to Theory
papers.abstract: The circular coordinates algorithm, a widely used tool in topological data analysis, relies on a lifting step to convert cocycles from a prime field to integer coefficients. We provide a rigorous analysis of this procedure, establishing a criterion for its success. We give an algebraic method for reducing the winding number under explicit torsion hypotheses. The torsion and coprimality hypotheses required by the winding number reduction are automatic in degree 1, because H^1(X; Z) is torsion-free. We extend these principles to homology, deriving analogous coefficientwise lifting criteria for cycles.

papers.title: Likelihood Geometry of Reflexive Polytopes
papers.abstract: We study the problem of maximum likelihood (ML) estimation for statistical models defined by reflexive polytopes. Our focus is on the maximum likelihood degree of these models as an algebraic measure of complexity of the corresponding optimization problem. We compute the ML degrees of all 4319 classes of three-dimensional reflexive polytopes, and observe some surprising behavior in terms of the presence of gaps between ML degrees and degrees of the associated toric varieties. We interpret these drops in the context of discriminants and prove formulas for the ML degree for families of reflexive polytopes, including the hypercube and its dual, the cross polytope, in arbitrary dimension. In particular, we determine a family of embeddings for the $d$-cube that implies ML degree one. Finally, we discuss generalized constructions of families of reflexive polytopes in terms of their ML degrees.

papers.title: Lower bounds for the gonality and the minimum density degree of modular curves
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with good reduction $C_0$ at a prime $p$, let $q$ be a power of $p$, and suppose that the $q$-power Frobenius agrees with an automorphism of $C_0$ at $S$ points. We prove that $C$ has only finitely many points of degree $d$ for every $d<S/(\sqrt q+1)^2$. In particular, the minimum density degree of $C$ is at least $\#C_0(\mathbb{F}_q)/(\sqrt q+1)^2$, and this bound can be sharp. Applying this, and the analogous bound $S/(q+1)$ for the gonality of the reduction of $C$, at the supersingular points of modular curves, we obtain lower bounds for the gonality and the minimum density degree of modular curves which are linear in the index. For every fixed prime $p$, the bound for the gonality also holds over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ for all modular curves in characteristic $p$, including those with Igusa level structure, which gives a lower bound linear in the index of the kind expected by Poonen. For example, $\operatorname{gon}_{\mathbb{C}} X_\Gamma\geq D/60$ for every congruence subgroup $\Gamma$ of index $D$ in $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and level not divisible by $6$, and this is sharp. As applications, we show that the non-CM points of degree $6$ on $X_1(37)$ have sporadic lifts to $X_1(N)$ for all $N$ divisible by $37$ and not divisible by $30$, answering a question of Bourdon, Ejder, Liu, Odumodu and Viray, and that the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-isogeny class of the elliptic curve 1225.b2 contains infinitely many $j$-invariants of sporadic points on the curves $X_1(N)$, answering a question of Bourdon and Najman.

papers.title: Marked Persistent Homology: Circuits and Bordisms
papers.abstract: The barcode of a persistence module does not determine the relations among prescribed cycles. We encode these relations by a filtration of kernels in fixed coordinates, whose circuits can ramify into overlapping families and later recombine, unlike the merge-tree structure of degree-zero persistence. The kernels recover the marked image module and admit simultaneous rational bordism realizations. An explicit planar Vietoris-Rips filtration exhibits the circuit changes and their surface fillings.

papers.title: Moderate deviations for stochastic gradient Langevin averages with a computed Poisson normalizer
papers.abstract: We establish a relative Gaussian tail approximation for time averages of stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics centered at the invariant mean of an associated modified diffusion. Self-normalization is achieved via the trajectory-averaged squared gradient of the corresponding Poisson solution. Under weak dissipativity, conditionally sub-Gaussian gradient noise, and uniform derivative bounds on the drift, covariance factor, and observable, the approximation holds uniformly up to a growing radius \(r\to\infty\) whenever \[ r^4\log(T+e)/T\to0,\qquad r^2\eta\to0,\qquad r\eta^\gamma\sqrt T\to0, \] where \(\eta\) denotes the step size and \(T=m\eta\) is the observation horizon. Here \(\gamma=1\) for the uncorrected empirical average and \(\gamma=2\) after removing the leading weak discretization bias. The proof controls the predictable quadratic variation under an exponential tilt of the full centered one-step Poisson increment. Given coefficient evaluations together with known growth and derivative bounds and an admissible positive dissipativity constant, we further construct finite-budget simulation procedures for both the normalizer and the weak-bias correction. To preserve relative Gaussian tail accuracy for the resulting confidence intervals, it suffices to control the relative error of the empirical energy to \(o(r^{-2})\) and the additive error of the corrected average to \(o((r\sqrt T)^{-1})\), with combined failure probability \(o(1-\Phi(r))\). The gradient noise is permitted to be asymmetric with a linearly growing covariance factor; in a linear Gaussian model, the excess variance induced by this noise alters the limiting tail ratio at the boundary radius \(r=c\eta^{-1/2}\) whenever \(\eta T\to\infty\).

papers.title: Moduli of non-pure sheaves and contractions of Hilbert schemes
papers.abstract: We define certain stacks of rank one sheaves on a smooth projective variety, and show that they admit proper good moduli spaces. We offer several applications to contractions of subschemes inside Hilbert schemes of points. We construct a surgery diagram via non-GIT wall-crossing, and use the interpretation of the surgery as a fine moduli of sheaves to prove instances Kawamata's DK-hypothesis in this setting.

papers.title: Monochromatic or rainbow triangles in three dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that every coloring of three-dimensional Euclidean space contains, for every prescribed nondegenerate triangle, a congruent copy whose vertices are either all of the same color or all of different colors. The set of colors is arbitrary and can be infinite. The proof is elementary. Its two geometric ingredients are an odd closed sequence obtained by moving among three concentric circles, and a finite sequence of equal-length steps joining any two points of a sphere.

papers.title: Monoidal analog of cluster-tilting theory and monoidal reachability of acyclic cluster algebras
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we prove that many analogous facts of cluster-tilting theory holds in monoidal categories from quantum affine algebras or quiver Hecke algebras. We show that a maximal commuting family of real prime modules, which is an analogous object of a cluster-tilting object, is always a laurent family introduced by Kashiwara-Kim-Oh-Park. By using $\widetilde{\Lambda}$-invariants, we construct an exchange matrix of each laurent family and show that a laurent family is always completely $\Lambda$-admissible monoidal seed. We obtain that a pair of real prime modules is an exchange pair if and only if $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is $1$.
  When the category is a monoidal categorification of a cluster algebra of acyclic type, we prove that $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is not less than generic Ext invariant by using tropical $F$-invariant introduced by Cao and Fei. Moreover, we show that, the conjecture asserting that real simple modules correspond exactly to cluster monomials holds in these cases.

papers.title: Multiplication by 2 and by 6 through products of Jacobians, and the Jacobian index of a very general abelian variety of dimension 4, 5 and 6
papers.abstract: For an abelian variety A over an algebraically closed field, let s_J(A) be the least positive integer n such that multiplication by n factors through a product of Jacobians of curves; s_J(A) = 1 exactly when A is a direct summand of such a product. We prove, in every characteristic, that multiplication by 2 factors through a product of Jacobians on every principally polarized abelian variety of dimension at most 5, and multiplication by 6 on every one of dimension 6; that s_J(A) divides gcd(2, δ(A)) for every abelian surface and gcd(6, δ(A)) for every abelian threefold, where δ(A) is the greatest common divisor of the Euler characteristics of line bundles on A. The known bound is (2g − 1)!. For a complex principally polarized A with minimal class γ = θ^{g−1}/(g − 1)!, let m(A) be the least positive multiple of γ that is the class of an algebraic cycle; Matsusaka's construction gives s_J(A) | m(A), and we prove m(A) | s_J(A)². With the theorems of Engel, de Gaay Fortman and Schreieder this gives the exact values s_J(A) = 2 for a very general principally polarized abelian variety of dimension 4 and 5, and s_J(A) = 6 in dimension 6; and every prime p ≤ g/2 divides s_J(A) in dimension g. Finally, s_J(A) is exactly the least integer n for which n times the inverse of the isomorphism H^{2g−1}(A)(g − 1) → H¹(Â) is induced by an integral algebraic cycle; this answers, for abelian varieties, the second question that Grothendieck asks on sheet 70 of cote 14 of his Montpellier archive. The results come from a run of GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and from Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max; they were checked and the text written by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max.

papers.title: Natural boundaries and real-point limits for class-one Goldbach series
papers.abstract: For integers $q,r\ge2$ we study the $r$-fold von Mangoldt Dirichlet series in which every summand is congruent to one modulo $q$. Under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis at modulus $q$, the known meromorphic continuation to $\Re s>r-1$ has the line $\Re s=r-1$ as a natural boundary. The proof allows multiple zeros, zeros shared by different Dirichlet $L$-functions, and coincident sums of ordinates. The character average for class one adds the multiplicities at each ordinate. This gives positive integer weights, up to a common factor, in a sum of Gamma products to which the integer phase cone applies. A normal limit recovers the combined coefficient of all pairs at a given point of the line. The higher-fold boundary follows by reducing to the binary series. Under GRH at modulus $q$, we also subtract a main term, explicit up to an entire function, and compute the positive normal limit at the real boundary point. For the unrestricted series under the Riemann Hypothesis we give the regularized limit at every ordinate, including the real point for $r\ge3$. Lean 4 checks the class-one results, with the character identity in pointwise form, and the unrestricted limits, taking the applicable classical estimates as premises.

papers.title: Nested-Ovals Fewnomial Systems: A Universal Two-Parameter Disproof of Kouchnirenko's Conjecture for All (t_1, t_2) >= (3, 3)
papers.abstract: For positive integers $t_1, \dots, t_n \ge 2$, let $\mathcal{S}_n(t_1, \dots, t_n)$ denote the maximum number of nondegenerate strictly positive real solutions of a square polynomial system $f_1(x) = \cdots = f_n(x) = 0$ where each $f_i$ has at most $t_i$ monomials, and write $\mathcal{S}(t_1, t_2) := \mathcal{S}_2(t_1, t_2)$. Kouchnirenko's 1975 conjecture posited $\mathcal{S}_n(t_1, \dots, t_n) \le \prod_{i=1}^n (t_i - 1)$. We introduce a nested-ovals curve family $f_1(u, v) = u + v - 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{t_1-3} (-1)^{k-1} L^{-k^2} (uv)^{-k} = 0$ coupled to an inductively constructed lower-envelope $t_2$-nomial $F_{t_2}(u, v) = 0$ with an asymmetric tail. We prove four results, all completely formalized in Lean 4 (v4.36.0, Mathlib4, 7,575 lines) with zero sorry, zero native_decide, and only the three standard axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]: (1) $\mathcal{S}(t_1, t_2) \ge t_1 t_2 - t_1 - 2 = (t_1 - 1)(t_2 - 1) + (t_2 - 3)$ for all $t_1 \ge 4, t_2 \ge 3$ (and $\mathcal{S}(3, t_2) \ge 3t_2 - 4$), raising the asymptotic slope in $t_2$ from $t_1 - 1$ to $t_1$ for every fixed $t_1 \ge 3$; (2) $\mathcal{S}(t, t) \ge t^2 - t - 2 = (t - 1)^2 + (t - 3) > (t - 1)^2$ for every $t \ge 4$; (3) $\mathcal{S}_n(t, \dots, t) \ge (t^2 - t - 2)^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} (t - 1)^{n \bmod 2}$ for all $n \ge 2$ and $t \ge 4$, yielding an exponential disproof of Kouchnirenko's conjecture for every fixed $t \ge 4$; (4) An explicit symmetric integer quadrinomial record $\mathcal{S}(4, 4) \ge 10$ and $B(2, 4) \ge 10$ (7 distinct shared monomials, degrees 12 and 47), certified via exact rational 2D Newton-Banach contraction in Lean 4, simultaneous Pandrosion-residue complex root certification (pandsysroots v0.34.0), and 520-digit verification, alongside 520-digit certified systems for $\mathcal{S}(4,5) \ge 14$, $\mathcal{S}(4,6) \ge 18$, $\mathcal{S}(5,5) \ge 17$, and $\mathcal{S}(5,6) \ge 22$.

papers.title: Nonzero central quotients of the Virasoro enveloping algebra are simple
papers.abstract:
We prove a conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra that the central quotient $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$ of the universal enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra is simple for all $c \neq 0$. We extend the result to the $N=1$ super-Virasoro algebras.
  Our proof reveals a new connection between enveloping algebras and polynomial identity algebras. Although the enveloping algebra itself does not satisfy a polynomial identity, the adjoint action on each filtered piece does satisfy a standard identity. In particular, the Witt algebra $W$, as an adjoint module over itself, satisfies the standard identity $\mathrm{St}_4$, whereas $\mathrm{Vir}$ fails by a nonzero multiple of the central charge. Propagating this gap through the PBW filtration of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$, for every nonscalar element, we construct an alternating adjoint operator that lowers its order by exactly one.
  As applications, we compute the annihilators of all representations with nonzero central character, prove a strengthened form of Etingof's conjecture on nonsplit extensions of $W$-modules, and reduce the classification of prime ideals of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})$ to those of $\mathrm{U}(W)$.

papers.title: Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on polarized manifolds
papers.abstract: In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system $T$ on the space of Fubini--Study metrics of a polarized manifold $(X,L)$, whose fixed points are the balanced metrics. In \cite{S}, Sano proves that the iterates of $T$ converge to a balanced metric, provided that a balanced metric exists and the automorphism group of $(X,L)$ is discrete modulo scalars. We remove the assumption on the automorphism group. Moreover, we show that the convergence is exponential with the optimal rate $\rho_*$ given by the linearization of $T$ at a balanced metric, which extends a result of Ioos and Polterovich (\cite{IP}) for discrete automorphism groups. We compute $\rho_*$ for $(\CP^n,\mathcal{O}(d))$ and $(\CP^1\times\CP^1,\mathcal{O}(d,d))$; for $\CP^1$ this confirms the rate obtained numerically by Sherman (\cite{Sh}).

papers.title: On $F$-thresholds of differential power filtrations
papers.abstract: We study the $F$-threshold of differential power filtrations of monomial ideals. We give the existence of this number and show that it is upper bounded by the maximum height of the minimal primes of the underlying monomial ideal. As an application of our results, we show that the dimension of the polynomial ring and the $F$-threshold of the differential power filtration of the monomial maximal ideal are the same.

papers.title: On a new resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group E(2)
papers.abstract: We provide a non-divergent resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group $E(2)$, replacing the integral on the whole group with the Haar measure by an invariant integration with non local kernels constructed by Steinberg and Wolf in 1981, valid for solutions of Helmholtz equation, that appears in natural way as the eigenvalue equation of the Casimir operator of $E(2)$. With this construction, all properties of Perelomov coherent states are preserved, in particular covariance, and all square-integrable functions are addmissible, improving previous results like those of de Bi\`evre and Torr\'esani.

papers.title: On Casagrande-Druel Fano varieties with Lefschetz defect 2
papers.abstract: The larger the Lefschetz defect delta(X) of a smooth complex Fano variety X, the more information we can deduce about the geometry of X. The structure of varieties with delta(X) greater than 2 is known. In this paper, we study the case delta(X)=2. In particular, we focus on Fano varieties with delta(X)=2 arising from the so called Casagrande-Druel construction, which we refer to as Construction A. We show that among the 19 families of Fano 3-folds with delta(X)=2 classified by Mori and Mukai, 15 arise from such construction. Moreover, we construct all Fano 4-folds with Picard number greater than 3 and delta(X)=2 admitting such a structure, obtaining 145 distinct families in total. This completes the classification of all Casagrande-Druel Fano 4-folds with delta(X)=2. To broaden the scope, we also study a generalized version of Construction A, which we call Construction B, and we show that 18 out of the 19 families of Fano 3-folds with delta(X)=2 arise from it.

papers.title: On dual varieties of smooth projective varieties
papers.abstract: For a smooth irreducible nondegenerate complex projective variety $X\subsetneq\mathbb P^N$, we prove that its projective dual $X^\vee$ is a hypersurface whenever $\operatorname{dim} X\ge3\operatorname{codim}X-2$. This result may be regarded as further evidence for Hartshorne's complete intersection conjecture. We also prove the duality defect conjecture of Landman in codimension at most five. Finally, we complete Ein's classification of smooth nondegenerate complex projective varieties with smooth projective dual. The list consists of smooth quadrics, the Segre varieties $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^m$ with $m\ge2$, the Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(2,5)$, and the spinor tenfold in $\mathbb P^{15}$.

papers.title: On generalized linear periods for inner forms of GLn
papers.abstract: Let $\mathrm{D}$ be a central division algebra of index $e$ over a non-Archimedean local field $\mathrm{F}$ of characteristic zero. For every integer $n\ge 1$ and every $s\in \mathbb{R}$, we classify the irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathrm{D})$ that admit a nonzero linear form transforming under the subgroup $\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathrm{D})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathrm{D})$ by the character $\nu^{es}\otimes\nu^{-es}$. We further show that such a linear form is unique up to scalars, and we characterize its existence in terms of Langlands parameters.

papers.title: On norm attainment, the absolute value and polar decomposition of bounded functionals on a $C^*$-algebra
papers.abstract: The absolute value of a bounded linear functional $\phi$ on a $C^*$-algebra $\mathfrak{A}$ is the noncommutative counterpart of the total variation of a complex measure. In the literature, it is usually constructed by considering the normal extension of $\phi$ to the bidual of $\mathfrak{A}$, and applying Sakai's polar decomposition to this extension. In this article, we provide a direct construction. As our main result, we prove that there is a unique functional $\rho$ on $\mathfrak{A}$ such that \[\|\phi(\,\cdot\,B)-\rho\|^2\le 2\|\phi\| \left( \|\phi\| - \Re\phi(B) \right) \; \textrm{ for every contraction } B \in \mathfrak{A},\] and moreover, $\rho$ is positive. We refer to $\rho$ as the absolute value of $\phi$, and denote it by $\abs{\phi}$. We further show that our definition agrees with the classical one. The right-hand side of the above inequality may be viewed as a measure of the failure of $\phi$ to attain its norm at $B$. When $\phi$ attains its norm at $A$, we get $|\phi|=\phi(\,\cdot\,A)$ and further show that $\phi=|\phi|(\,\cdot\,A^*)$. In general, we obtain an approximate polar decomposition of $\phi$ with the help of norming sequences. From this we deduce Sakai's theorem, the Banach-space identification of $\mathfrak{A}^{**}$ with the enveloping von Neumann algebra, and the Jordan decomposition of a hermitian functional. The organizing principle is an elementary fact about discs in the unit ball of $\mathfrak{A}$: if $Z+\lambda D$ lies in the unit ball whenever $|\lambda|\le1$, then $|\phi(Z)|+ |\phi(D)|\le \|\phi\|$. In particular, a functional which attains its norm at $Z$ vanishes at $D$. We use four explicit discs: two of them lead to the results above, and the other two give a new proof of Kadison's characterization of the extreme points of the unit ball of $\mathfrak{A}$. To the best of our knowledge, the above characterization of the absolute value without the bidual, and the polar factorization at arbitrary norming contractions, do not appear in this form in the literature. We hope that the elementary approach taken here may be of use in a first course on operator algebras.

papers.title: On the Gorenstein property of local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$
papers.abstract: Local models are used to model, \'etale-locally, the singularities of integral models of Shimura varieties. They are defined in terms of linear algebra and admit explicit descriptions by matrix equations. We determine exactly which local models for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ are Gorenstein. On one hand, this gives the analogous information for integral models of Shimura varieties for unramified unitary groups with parahoric level structure, and on the other hand also results in certain natural matrix equations defining non-Gorenstein singularities.

papers.title: On the Hermitian K-theory of Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We compute the $\mathbb{G}W$-spectrum (Karoubi--Grothendieck--Witt spectrum) of Grassmannians over divisorial schemes defined over fields of characteristic zero, and, as a corollary, determine their stabilized $\mathbb{L}$-theory spectrum. As part of our computation, we establish split fibration sequences in $\mathbb{K}$-theory, $\mathbb{G}W$-theory and $\mathbb{L}$-theory.

papers.title: On the Hodge theory of toroidal embeddings and corresponding vanishings
papers.abstract: We prove $E_1$-degeneration of the logarithmic Hodge--de Rham spectral sequence for proper toroidal triples. For a compatible Weil divisor, we realize the associated twisted logarithmic de Rham complex as the filtered de Rham complex of an object in the bounded derived category of mixed Hodge modules. We use this realization to prove a vanishing theorem of Kawamata--Viehweg type for toroidal triples. We also prove relative Bott vanishing in the toric case.
