On the local toric charts of a toroidal triple $(X,!B,*C)$, we characterize when the canonical exchange morphism between the two ordered extensions of the constant sheaf on $X\setminus(B+C)$ is an isomorphism, when each order recovers the logarithmic de Rham complex, and when this complex is perverse.

papers.title: On the homotopy types of $4$-dimensional toric orbifolds
papers.abstract: The cohomological rigidity problem for toric orbifolds asks when an integral cohomology isomorphism implies a homotopy equivalence. In this paper we reformulate the cohomological rigidity problem in the context of $4$-dimensional toric orbifolds by introducing what we call proper isomorphisms, a variant of a concept studied by J.H.C. Whitehead. We prove that each proper isomorphism class of $4$-dimensional toric orbifolds contains at most two distinct homotopy types, and that the two classifications agree in certain special circumstances.

papers.title: On the splitting of surfaces in motivic stable homotopy category
papers.abstract: Over a perfect field of characteristic zero, we study when the top cell splits off from a pointed smooth projective surface in motivic stable homotopy, with K3 surfaces as the main example. Adams--Riemann--Roch and the motivic Adams relations give a uniform top-codimension annihilator. This yields an integral extreme-cell splitting in particular for complex projective K3 surfaces. Chow--Witt correspondences also yield noncanonical three-term decompositions of Milnor--Witt motives with extreme Tate summands and a nilpotence criterion for lifting finite systems of Chow projectors. In positive characteristic, the annihilator statement holds after inverting the characteristic.

papers.title: Partial $F$-invariants and cluster categorifications
papers.abstract: The $F$-invariant in cluster algebras is a combinatorial invariant that unifies the $E$-invariant from additive categorification and the $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant from monoidal categorification. In this paper, we study its refinement, the partial $F$-invariant, and establish its mutation formula under changes of the initial seed. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Reading, which asserts that the non-compatible cluster variables can be separated by sign-coherence of $g$-vectors upon varying the initial seed. We further show that, for cluster monomials, the partial $F$-invariants coincide with both the partial $E$-invariants for reachable decorated representations of quivers with potentials and the pole orders of normalized $R$-matrices (or partial $\mathfrak{d}$-invariants) for finite-dimensional reachable simple modules over quantum affine algebras. As consequences, we obtain a combinatorial formula for the pole orders for reachable simple modules in terms of $q$-characters; we verify the conjectural explicit formula for the pole orders between Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules.

papers.title: Phase cones for Gamma-weighted atoms of additive Dirichlet series
papers.abstract: In the continuation of an additive Dirichlet series, several pairs of zeros can contribute to the same candidate singularity. The numerators are products of Gamma values with complex coefficients, so the sum of the numerators, which we call the atom, can vanish. We prove a uniform non-cancellation theorem for these sums. Stirling's formula uniformly on fixed vertical strips is a classical theorem, taken as an explicit premise. The pairs have the form $b+i(u+\tau)$ and $c-iu$, with bounded $\tau$, constant $b+c$, and real parts in $[1-B,B]$, where $1/2\le B<1$. The coefficients lie in a common sector of half-angle $\delta<\pi(1-B)$. Every unit bin of heights is finite, and the total coefficient mass in every unit bin with nonnegative base satisfies a uniform polynomial growth bound in that base. The weighted Gamma sum converges absolutely and is nonzero if the least height is sufficiently large and a coefficient there has modulus bounded below. The height threshold depends only on the bounds in the hypotheses. After a common rotation every nonzero head term, at a height close to the least height, has positive projection on the real axis. Exponential decay bounds the sum of the remaining terms. The angle restriction is sharp. We recover the integer-weight cone of the author's earlier paper on the Goldbach generating series. We also explain the two ways a nonzero atom is used. A nonzero atom gives an interior pole where the candidate points are locally finite and both the correction and $\Gamma$ are regular at the point. Gamma regularity is automatic for sums with positive real part. When the remaining pair sums lie on the boundary line and their numerators are absolutely summable, a nonzero atom gives a nonzero normal limit of the corrected series. The sector theorem and its two specializations have been checked in Lean 4 with Stirling on strips as an explicit premise.

papers.title: Primitive Collections for Klyachko Varieties
papers.abstract: Klyachko introduced a family of $S_m\times S_n$-invariant toric Gorenstein Fano varieties, $X_{mn}$, with connections to representation theory, algebraic groups, and graph theory. He focused on the case in which $m$ and $n$ are coprime, for which $X_{mn}$ are smooth, and hence Fano. Klyachko and Voskresenskii later proved that all forms of $X_{mn}$ are stably rational when $m, n$ are coprime, and that all forms of $X_{mn}$ are rational when $n$ is congruent to 1 modulo $m$. In the same paper, they classified centrally symmetric toric Fano varieties as products of projective lines and generalized del Pezzo varieties, $X_{2,2k+1}$. For this reason, the special case of generalized del Pezzo varieties are frequently studied. For example, Ballard, Duncan, and McFadden proved that the bounded derived category of generalized del Pezzo varieties has a full exceptional collection of line bundles. An understanding of the maximal cones and primitive collections of the fan associated to $X_{2,2k+1}$ is crucial in their construction. In this paper, we focus on the Klyachko varieties $X_{mn}$ in the case in which $n$ is congruent to 1 modulo $m$. We determine a description of the maximal cones and primitive collections for the associated fan. We also determine a description of their cohomology ring and some stability results on the $S_m\times S_n$-orbits of maximal cones and primitive collections for $X_{mn}$.

papers.title: Proper kernels in microlocal sheaf theory
papers.abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be real analytic manifolds and let $\Lambda \subseteq T^*X$ and $\Sigma \subseteq T^*Y$ be closed conic subanalytic singular isotropics. Given a sheaf $K \in \mathrm{Sh}_{-\Lambda \times \Sigma}(X \times Y)$ microsupported in $-\Lambda \times \Sigma$, consider the convolution functor $(-) \ast K \colon \mathrm{Sh}_{\Lambda}(X) \rightarrow \mathrm{Sh}_{\Sigma}(Y)$ from sheaves microsupported in $\Lambda$ to sheaves microsupported in $\Sigma$. We show that the convolution functor $(-) \ast K$ preserves compact objects if and only if for each $x \in X$, the restriction $K|_{\{x\} \times Y} \in \mathrm{Sh}_\Sigma(Y)$ is a compact object. By a result of Kuo-Li, the functor sending a sheaf kernel $K$ to the convolution functor $(-) \ast K$ is an equivalence between the category $\mathrm{Sh}_{-\Lambda \times \Sigma}(X \times Y)$ of sheaves microsupported in $-\Lambda \times \Sigma$ and the category of cocontinuous functors from $\mathrm{Sh}_\Lambda(X)$ to $\mathrm{Sh}_\Sigma(Y)$. We therefore classify all cocontinuous functors that preserve compact objects between the two categories. Our approach is entirely categorical and requires minimal input from geometry: we introduce the notion of a proper object in a compactly generated stable infinity-category and study its properties under strongly continuous localizations to obtain the result. The main geometric input is the analysis of compact and proper objects of the category of $P$-constructible sheaves for a triangulation $P$ of a manifold $Z$ via the exit path category $\mathrm{Exit}(Z, P) \simeq P$. Along the way, we show that a sheaf $F \in \mathrm{Sh}_\Lambda(X)$ is proper if and only if it has perfect stalks, which is equivalent to a result of Nadler.

papers.title: Quot schemes on projective space
papers.abstract: We develop general methods for studying Quot schemes on projective space, including a new construction of components with no common neighbours. We show that the radius of Hilbert and Quot schemes can grow linearly with the dimension of the subschemes being parametrized, and construct the first examples of Hilbert schemes of curves with radius two. For absolutely split bundles on projective space, we construct a distinguished generically smooth component and classify all smooth Quot schemes. In most cases, we give explicit geometric descriptions in terms of products of generalized flag varieties and projective bundles over Grassmannians.

papers.title: Ramification divisors and twisted Nambu brackets of Keller maps
papers.abstract: For a polynomial map $\phi\colon\A^n\to\A^n$ we study the Yau twist of the Jacobian Nambu bracket by $\phi^*$. The Hamiltonian fields of pulled back functions span the image of the adjugate of $d\phi$, so the twist detects the ramification divisor of $\phi$. For a Keller map $F$ the twist is removable exactly when $F$ is an automorphism; otherwise $F$ is not proper, and every projective extension of $F$ has a non-zero effective ramification divisor supported on the boundary, whose image is the non-properness set. These results apply to every counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture and to families of Keller maps. For the explicit three-dimensional counterexample we show that $\A^3$ is the variety of binary cubic forms of a special shape with a marked simple root, and that $F$ forgets the root. This gives the degree, the fibres, the non-properness set, the monodromy and the structure of the twisted ternary algebra. Three examples modelled on weighted scrolls illustrate equivariance, degeneration to an automorphism, and an $A_1$ singularity of the fibre.

papers.title: Rational Numerals and Carry Geometry in Iteris
papers.abstract: Iteris is a positional notation in base 10^4. It writes each four-digit decimal block as a Cistercian-inspired glyph and arranges the glyphs in a horizontal row. We specify a canonical representation of every rational number and determine the lengths of its fractional prefix and repeating block cycle. The graph of legal single-stroke edits in a quadrant is an isometric subgraph of a five-dimensional binary cube. The Cartesian product of these quadrant graphs makes node distances additive. We derive the exact distribution of decimal carry costs on words of m decimal digits, including leading zeros as needed to fill the width. Stroke parity rules out a one-stroke ordering of all 10^m words. A construction attains the minimum total edit cost 10^m+2^m-2 for an open order. For the four positions of one node the open minimum is 10,014 and numerical order costs 19,986.

papers.title: Reading Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: On 20 November 2026, Levent Alpöge released a Lean formalization of an announced proof of the Riemann hypothesis. This paper provides an illustrated introduction to its mathematical ideas for mathematicians outside number theory. We interpret the proof through Chebyshev’s classical principle, organizing its main ideas around three mechanisms: divisibility, amplification and cost control. These are realized through height-two formal groups, a tower of theta lifts, and bounds for Tate-Shafarevich groups. Elementary examples and conceptual diagrams illustrate how these ingredients interact to achieve square-root accuracy in prime sums. We also present a conditional reduction checked in Lean and raise several questions concerning possible simplifications of the proof and applications beyond the Riemann hypothesis. This AI-assisted exposition aims at mathematical understanding rather than completeness or independent verification.

papers.title: Reflection subgroups and the Lookup Conjecture
papers.abstract:
The Lookup Conjecture of Boe-Graham proposes a Bruhat graph criterion for rational smoothness of Schubert varieties in the flag variety $\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{B}$ of a complex reductive group. Its extension to Kac-Moody groups of affine type $\widetilde{A}_n$ was considered by Graham-Li. We prove the original conjecture as well as its extension to $\widetilde{A}_n$. Our method could be applied more generally to any Kac-Moody group after checking the rank-three reflection subgroups of its Weyl group.
  We also prove a parabolic version of the Lookup Conjecture for the type $A$ affine Grassmannian, where a stronger Bruhat graph degree monotonicity property in fact holds, and discuss the implication via the geometric Satake correspondence for weight multiplicities.

papers.title: Regularity Criteria for Ind-Sheaves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the Kashiwara-Schapira regularity conjecture [Conjecture 6.4, Masaki Kashiwara and Pierre Schapira, Microlocal study of ind-sheaves I: micro-support and regularity, 2003] in arbitrary dimension. For this purpose, we show that under suitable finiteness and isotropic micro-support conditions, ind-sheaves which are regular on the zero section come from $\mathbb{R}$-constructible sheaves. Furthermore, we characterize the essential image of constructible sheaves under the natural embedding functor, and relate them to regular holonomic $\mathcal{D}$-modules via the regular Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. Moreover, we present a non-characteristic deformation lemma and a microlocal Morse lemma for regular ind-sheaves as an application of the main theorem.

papers.title: Representations of $p$-adic reductive groups
Residual indices of fixed multiplicative subgroups over number fields: power savings and moment obstructions
papers.abstract: The residual index of a multiplicative group at a good prime ideal is the index of its reduction in the multiplicative residue group. For a fixed finitely generated group of rank \(r\) over a number field, we prove a power-saving estimate for the full index distribution up to norm \(X\), with errors weighted by \(t^\sigma\), where \(t\) is the index. The estimate is uniform in a Frobenius restriction in a fixed finite Galois extension and allows torsion. Under the generalized Riemann hypothesis it holds for \(r\ge2\) and \(0\le\sigma<(r-1)/(r+2)\). More generally, it follows from a common bound below \(r/(r+1)\) for the real parts of the nontrivial zeta zeros of the relevant division-field composita. Model moments are finite unconditionally for positive orders below \(r\), and empirical moments converge in the proved weight range. We also give unconditional counterexamples to Ambrose's number-field generalization of Wagstaff's moment heuristic for fixed groups, using the unrestricted count over all residue degrees. For rational generators of rank \(r>1\) in a nontrivial finite Galois extension of \(\mathbb{Q}\), the contribution of each occurring residue degree \(f>1\) contradicts the proposed scales at moment orders \(1<s<1+f(r-1)\). Higher-degree ideals have relative density zero, but their normalized first-moment tails carry a positive contribution, which diverges in rank one. Two rank-three groups over \(\mathbb{Q}(i)\), including a group of norm one that generates the field, have second-moment sums at least of order \(X^{3/2}/\log X\). For \(\langle2,3,5\rangle\), the lower-bound coefficient is \(655\zeta(3)/(14\pi^4)\), where \(\zeta\) is the Riemann zeta function.

papers.title: Sectional category versus module sectional category for retractive maps
papers.abstract: We construct a map between simply connected rational spaces of finite rational type which admits a homotopy retraction and satisfies $msecat(p)=2<secat(p)=3$. The target is the rationalization of a simply connected twelve-dimensional CW complex with eleven cells, and is rationally hyperbolic. This disproves Carrasquel--Vera's conjecture for retractive maps.

papers.title: Self-normalized moderate deviations for stochastic gradient Langevin averages with variance correction
papers.abstract: We prove a two-sided relative Gaussian tail approximation for bias-corrected time averages of stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics. The target is the invariant mean of the modified diffusion. From independent stochastic-gradient samples, values of the observable, and known model bounds, we estimate the first weak-bias term and the conditional variance per unit time of a Poisson increment. The variance estimate is nonnegative and includes the full first-order correction. Suppose that the drift is smooth and strongly dissipative and that the gradient noise is state-independent, of the form $B+\tau G$, where $B$ is bounded and centered and $G$ is an independent standard Gaussian vector. As $\eta\downarrow0$, $T=m\eta\to\infty$, and $r\to\infty$, the approximation holds uniformly for $0\le x\le r$ if \[ r^4\log(T+e)/T\to0,\qquad r\eta^2\sqrt T\to0. \] It suffices to estimate the variance to relative error $o(r^{-2})$ and the corrected average to additive error $o((r\sqrt T)^{-1})$, with combined failure probability $o(1-\Phi(r))$. An explicit observation schedule permits $r=o(\eta^{-2/3}[\log(1/\eta)]^{-1/6})$. The proof controls the original predictable quadratic variation under exponential tilting through a discrete Poisson equation. A residual bound for the diffusion Poisson equation gives a finite construction from gradient samples. This bound also applies to weakly dissipative drifts and state-dependent innovations with known local fourth-moment bounds. For fixed dimension and model bounds, the oracle sample count is polynomial in the trajectory radius, inverse tolerances, and the logarithms of the inverse failure probabilities, up to a factor $m$. For additive isotropic Gaussian innovations and evaluable coefficients, paired Euler paths also give polynomial auxiliary operation counts.

papers.title: Semiorthogonal decompositions of limit categories for symmetric stacks
papers.abstract:
In our earlier work with Tudor Padurariu, we introduced the notion of limit categories for derived stacks with self-dual cotangent complexes and used them to formulate the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture. In this paper, we generalize the notion of limit categories to a broader class of derived stacks, which we call symmetric stacks.
  One of the motivations for this generalization is to formulate Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type correspondences for a broader class of moduli stacks. We establish several fundamental properties of limit categories for symmetric stacks, including compact generation, the existence of semiorthogonal decompositions, functoriality, and a Kunneth formula.
  In a companion paper, we apply the results of this paper to formulate a Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for moduli stacks of sheaves on smooth surfaces with nef anticanonical divisors.

papers.title: Simple ordinary geometrically split abelian varieties over finite fields
papers.abstract: In this paper we provide a partial classification (necessary conditions) for all possible simple ordinary geometrically split abelian varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Let $A$ be such an abelian variety, i.e. $A$ is simple over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and splits as $A \sim B^s$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^d}$ for some simple abelian variety $B$. Assume that $d$ is a minimal extension degree over which $A$ splits and $B$ has a minimal field of definition (up to isogeny) $\mathbb{F}_{q^e}\subseteq \mathbb{F}_{q^d}$. For dimension $2$, Howe and Zhu showed that the only possible degrees $d$ are $2$, $3$, $4$, and $6$. Moreover, for each such degree $d$, they provided explicit formulae expressing the isogeny invariant, namely the characteristic polynomial of the Frobenius endomorphism $\chi_{A,q}$, in terms of the coeffients of $\chi_{B,q}$. We extend this result to ordinary abelian varieties of higher dimension. For dimensions $3$--$10$, we provide complete lists of such varieties as components of the Weil restriction $W_{\mathbb{F}_{q^d}/\mathbb{F}_q}(B)$ together with all possible triples $(d, e, s)$ and restrictions on characteristic polynomial $\chi_{A,q}$ of the form $\chi_{A, q} \mid \chi_{V, q}$. Here, $V$ is a component of Weil restriction $W_{\mathbb{F}_{q^d}/\mathbb{F}_q}(B)$ containing $A$ as an isogeny factor and having explicit expression of the characteristic polynomial $\chi_{V,q}$ in terms of coefficients of $\chi_{B,q^e}$. For higher dimensions, we propose an algorithm for enumeration of all possible cases for a given dimension of $A$. We also provide an implementation of this algorithm.

papers.title: Singularities in global pluripotential theory
papers.abstract: This book is an expanded version of the author's lecture notes at the Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics (IASM) at Zhejiang University. We systematically develop the theory of plurisubharmonic singularities on compact K\"ahler manifolds and relate it to the non-Archimedean pluripotential theory and toric pluripotential theory.

papers.title: Spectral Fluctuations and Occupation Memory in the Mass-Deformed SYK Model
papers.abstract: In the mass-deformed Sachdev–Ye–Kitaev model, fluctuations in the norms of the quadratic and quartic couplings change both the spectral width and the effective deformation. Fixing these norms removes the order-$t^4$ variance of the normalized, unfiltered trace. At fixed even $N\geq14$ we compute the surviving $t^6$ coefficient and the $t^8$ coefficient at the quadratic endpoint. Nested sampling at $N=14,18$ gives a positive estimate of the radius-averaged directional fourth cumulant of the filtered trace at $\kappa=4$ and $t=4,16$. Radial averaging gives a convolution in log coupling for scale-invariant observables, with a derivative bound sharp over all bounded responses. For the fixed-radius spacing ratio, the half-response coupling increases from $8.46$ at $N=10$ to $29.29$ at $N=22$. For quadratic normal-mode charges, dephasing determines the conserved weight, and two exact frequency moments bound the Laplace-averaged inelastic memory. In an isolated-pair ensemble with a regular detuning density at resonance, the mean elastic deficit is asymptotic to a constant times $\kappa^{-1}$. The inelastic curvature time grows as $\kappa^{1/2}$, while the time to a fixed fractional loss is of order $\kappa$. In the full model at $N=22$, summing the pair contributions gives $97.1\%$ of the measured elastic deficit at $\kappa=2048$. At $\kappa=64$ the normalized inelastic memory differs from the pair prediction by about $0.20$ at an intermediate time.

papers.title: Spectral reciprocity for reductive groups
papers.abstract:
For every finite subgroup $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{SU}(2)$, every connected compact or connected complex reductive group $G$, and every finite central subgroup $B\subset Z(G)$, we construct a degree-preserving linear Fourier isomorphism between the polynomial class modules of $(G,B)$ and $((G/B)^\vee,\widehat B)$. The transform exchanges central twists with characters of the actual grades and preserves the invariant polynomial contributions of the full centralizers. In degree zero it yields central-coefficient reciprocity under the Poincar\'e pairing on $S^3/\Gamma$.
  In particular, $\Gamma$ admits equally many conjugacy classes of homomorphisms into $G$ and its Langlands dual, which verifies a conjecture of Kojima and Tachikawa.

papers.title: Spherical structures on fusion categories of rank six
papers.abstract: Every complex fusion category of rank six admits a spherical structure. For a fusion category of arbitrary rank, central induction places the formal codegrees of its sphericalization in the field generated by its Frobenius–Perron dimension. It also compares the ordinary and spherical dimensions on a common family of objects. Equality on these objects gives a fusion subcategory on which the spherical structure descends. In rank six, bounds on the Fourier coefficients of the reciprocal codegrees and integral trace identities for the dimension ratio restrict the remaining dimension fields. The last quadratic case uses a Morita dual.

papers.title: Splitting of abelian varieties in motivic stable homotopy category
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss the motivic stable homotopy type of abelian varieties. For an abelian variety over a perfect field $k$, a top-dimensional cell always splits off in the motivic stable homotopy category $\text{SH}(k)$. Let $k=\mathbb{R}$. If $X$ is a real abelian variety of positive dimension $g$, there is, for $\mathbb{Z}[1/(2g)!]\subset\Lambda\subset\mathbb{Q}$, a concrete splitting in $\text{SH}(\mathbb{R})_\Lambda$ determined by the Deninger--Murre decomposition of the motive of $X$ and the real points $X(\mathbb{R})$. With rational coefficients, we also discuss its refinement from the viewpoint of K\"unnemann's Lefschetz decomposition.

papers.title: Splitting of multiplicity spaces into symmetric and alternating parts
Stability in abstract classes via set theoretic techniques
papers.abstract:
We prove that all abstract classes equipped with an independence relation satisfying a mild local character condition are stable. We obtain the result by using methods from model theory and set theory.
  We have several applications in the context of abstract classes of modules. In particular, we prove that if $K$ is a class of $R$-modules closed under isomorphisms and pure submodules and $\lambda^{\operatorname{card}(R) + \aleph_0} = \lambda$, then $K$ equipped with pure embeddings is stable in $\lambda$.

papers.title: Streamlining Three Recent Proofs of the Reinhardt Conjecture
papers.abstract: The Reinhardt Conjecture states that, among centrally symmetric planar convex disks, the smoothed regular octagon minimizes the density of the densest packing, with equality precisely for its invertible affine images. Three long proofs were announced in November 2026, by The-Anh Vu-Le, Lucas Schmutz, and Fei Xue. Our purpose is to streamline these proofs by combining their ideas in a single argument.

papers.title: Tate classes in prime dimension
papers.abstract: Let \(A\) be a geometrically simple abelian variety of odd prime dimension over a finitely generated field of characteristic \(p>0\), and assume that \(A\) is nonconstant up to isogeny. For every \(\ell\ne p\), its rational Tate classes are generated by divisors, with a possible exception in dimension seven for definite quaternionic multiplication and \(G_2\) monodromy. In specified endomorphism cases the result holds on every self-power. The proof recognizes one-dimensional tensor directions from the multiplicities in a Frobenius weight polytope. This identifies a Frobenius-stable adjoint subisocrystal and allows its Newton slopes to rule out certain tensor product representations.

papers.title: Tensor ideals of oligomorphic permutation categories
papers.abstract: We classify tensor ideals for oligomorphic permutation categories $Perm(G,\mu)$. To this end we define an equivalence relation on the class of transitive smooth $G$-sets. We show that there is a bijection between the tensor ideals of $Perm(G,\mu)$ and the downward-closed subsets of the poset of equivalence classes. As a corollary we obtain that there is a bijection between tensor ideals and thick tensor ideals. We determine the poset in many cases (mostly in characteristic $0$): the infinite symmetric group, wreath products, products of oligomorphic groups, equivariantizations, finite groups in positive characteristic and the classical groups $GL, O, Sp, U$ over a finite field.

papers.title: The $d$-gonal locus in the moduli space of tropical plane curves
papers.abstract: We introduce and study the locus $\mathbb{M}_{g,d}^\textrm{nd}$ of genus $g$ tropical plane curves of gonality $d$ inside the moduli space $\mathbb{M}^{\textrm{nd}}_{g}$ of tropical plane curves of genus $g$. Each such tropical curve arises from a Newton polygon, and we conjecture that the gonality of the tropical curve is equal to an easily computed parameter of this polygon called the expected gonality, closely related to the lattice width of the polygon. Let $\mathbb{M}_{g,{\underline{d}}}^\textrm{nd}$ denote the locus of tropical curves whose associated Newton polygon has expected gonality $d$. We prove that for fixed $d$ and sufficiently large genus $g$, the dimensions of these two loci agree: \[ \\dim\left(\mathbb{M}_{g,d}^\textrm{nd}\right) =\dim\left(\mathbb{M}_{g,{\underline{d}}}^\textrm{nd}\right). \] Our results provide evidence that, in sufficiently high genus compared to expected gonality, the gonality of a tropical curve is determined by the expected gonality of the Newton polygon from which it arises. We also leverage our results to prove bounds on the dimensions of moduli spaces of non-degenerate algebraic curves.

papers.title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected
papers.abstract:
We prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order $k \geq 3$: every spectral point is connected by a path to every "one leg versus the rest" flattening rank. In particular, the asymptotic spectrum evaluated at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen. This was previously known only on specific families of tensors (Strassen, FOCS 1986, Crelle 1987-1991; Wigderson and Zuiddam, Bull. AMS 2026) or for specific families of spectral points (Christandl, Vrana and Zuiddam, STOC 2018; Sakabe, Do\u{g}an and Walter, FOCS 2026; Alman, Li and Pratt, FOCS 2026).
  To obtain our path-connectedness theorem we develop a general method for "interpolating" between spectral points, which applies to Strassen semirings that are appropriately decomposable (in the sense of an information-theoretic "method of types" on the semiring) and whose spectral points satisfy a cover property (inspired by slice rank). This covers tensors and asymptotic rank (with "types" given by decomposition into symmetric group irreps), as well as other objects and asymptotic problems, like graphs and Shannon capacity, where it matches the interpolation of Vrana (2019).
  Using our interpolation methods we furthermore obtain new results and simpler proofs of previous results regarding the asymptotic spectrum of rectangular matrix multiplication, polynomial multiplication and non-crossing (laminar) quantum functionals.

papers.title: The asymptotics of maximal rank of three-way tensors
papers.abstract: We prove that the maximal rank of an $n\times n\times n$ tensor is $n^2/3+O(n^{3/2})$, over the real numbers and over every algebraically closed field. More generally, in format $\lfloor an\rfloor\times\lfloor bn\rfloor\times\lfloor cn\rfloor$, with $a,b,c>0$ fixed, the leading term is $\frac{abc}{a+b+c}n^2$. The argument starts with a criterion for rank with respect to an arbitrary projective variety: a decomposition of zero with surjective differential, from a smooth parameter space, bounds the rank of every point. For Segre varieties, we construct such decompositions using a basis of units in a split algebra. We also give an optimized finite bound and a closed estimate with explicit constants for the maximal rank.

papers.title: The border rank of the five-row permanent
papers.abstract: The five-row permanent has geometric Segre border rank sixteen in characteristic zero and in characteristic two. This settles the five-row case of a question of Han and Song. A degeneration of length fifteen would give compatible subspaces in a product of Grassmannians over the integers. In characteristic two the permanent becomes the determinant, so a common Borel subgroup fixes one such collection. The pair spaces admit six types. On the remaining slot sets, initial coordinates of the subspaces must satisfy implications induced by elementary substitutions and contractions. Two finite Boolean certificates exclude every pair assignment. Properness transfers the obstruction to characteristic zero.

papers.title: The border Waring rank of powers of a square-free monomial
papers.abstract: For all $n,d\ge2$, the geometric border Waring rank of $(x_1\cdots x_n)^{d-1}$ in characteristic zero is $d^{n-1}$. Flag-orbit flattenings and digit projections certify the lower bound. In the auxiliary characteristic, Frobenius makes the tensor invariant under the special linear group, and the flattening carries a highest flag vector to the next one. A nonzero integral minor transfers this bound to characteristic zero at prime-power heights. Splitting the multiplicities into digits multiplies these linear rank bounds and gives the formula at every height. A Schur-complement step propagates sharp certificates to unequal exponents in two directions. Normalized matching determines the border Waring rank when two exponents are sufficiently large compared with all the others. A strict growth argument also gives the conjectured value for every four-variable monomial with a linear factor.

papers.title: The Brauer--Manin obstruction to weak approximation on a constant K3 surface
papers.abstract: We construct a constant supersingular K3 surface over every global field of characteristic two for which rational points are Zariski dense but are not dense in the Brauer--Manin set. This shows that the analogue of Skorobogatov's conjecture over global function fields does not hold for supersingular K3 surfaces.

papers.title: The Classification of 3+1d Symmetry Enriched Topological Order
papers.abstract: We use a 2-categorical version of (de-)equivariantization to classify (3+1)d topological orders with a finite $G$-symmetry. In particular, we argue that (3+1)d fermionic topological order with $G$-symmetry correspond to $\mathbf{2SVect}$-enriched $G$-crossed braided fusion 2-categories. We then show that the categorical data necessary to define these theories agrees with that arising from a fermionic generalization of the Wang-Wen-Witten construction of bosonic topological theories with $G$-symmetry saturating an anomaly. More generally, we also explain how 2-categorical (de-) equivariantization yields a classification of all braided fusion 2-categories.

papers.title: The Complexity of Choosing Local Bases for Zero-Error Quantum Readout
papers.abstract: A graph compactly specifies a quantum memory. Its edges carry parities of vertex bits. Some parities are recorded as exact classical flags, while each remaining pair of edges selects one of four pure qubit states in two mutually unbiased bases. We ask whether one copy identifies the vertex word up to global inversion when each party fixes its measurement after learning the flags. Choosing suitable bases is $\Sigma_2^P$-complete. Checking specified bases is coNP-complete. Both results hold on simple bipartite graphs of maximum degree three whose data edges form a matching and whose flags form disjoint paths. Every instance in both reductions has a perfect adaptive decoder using a single additional broadcast bit to choose the data measurements. For unrestricted collective readout, the complementary problem is Conflict-Free Cut with paired edges, which gives a published source of its hardness. We also give a finite decision tree for adaptive local readout and report two exhaustive enumerations through six labelled vertices.

papers.title: The dimension of a Euclidean space is determined by the isomorphic structure of its Lipschitz-free space
papers.abstract: We prove that the real Lipschitz-free space $\F(\R^m)$ embeds isomorphically into $\F(\R^n)$ if and only if $m\leq n$. Consequently, the Lipschitz-free spaces over Euclidean spaces of different positive dimensions are not linearly isomorphic.

papers.title: The Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for smooth surfaces
papers.abstract:
Using a general theory of limit categories for symmetric stacks, we construct their semiorthogonal decompositions for moduli stacks of pure one-dimensional coherent sheaves on smooth surfaces with nef anti-canonical divisors. The components of these semiorthogonal decompositions are quasi-BPS categories associated with the corresponding local Calabi--Yau threefolds.
  By comparing these semiorthogonal decompositions with those of dg-categories of coherent sheaves on moduli stacks of semistable sheaves, we propose a Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for surfaces, generalizing the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture for $\GL_r$-Higgs bundles. Our conjecture includes a correspondence for Higgs bundles twisted by sufficiently ample line bundles on curves.
  We discuss examples and construct Hecke actions on limit categories and, under certain conditions, on quasi-BPS categories. For symplectic surfaces, these actions are expected to provide a categorical lift of the corresponding Hecke operators on BPS cohomology constructed by Davison--Hennecart--Kinjo--Schiffmann--Vasserot.

papers.title: The Esperet–Hendrey–Lagoutte–Marseloo–Norin–Steiner (2025) flow reconfiguration problem has a positive answer
papers.abstract: For a finite multigraph $G$ and an integer $k\ge 2$, let $M_k(G)$ be the graph on the nowhere-zero $\mathbb{Z}_k$-flows of $G$, and $I_k(G)$ the graph on the integer flows $F$ of $G$ with $1\le|F(e)|\le k-1$ on every edge; two flows are adjacent if the support of their difference is a cycle. We prove that $M_k(G)$ and $I_k(G)$ are connected for every finite bridgeless loopless multigraph $G$ if $k=40$, if $k=48$, or if $k$ is a multiple of $4$ with $k\ge 52$. This gives a positive answer to Problem 1.2 of Esperet, Hendrey, Lagoutte, Marseloo, Norin and Steiner. The same holds for $k=66$, for every prime power $p^N$ with $N\ge 6$, and for a set of moduli of natural density one; these results do not cover every $k\ge 40$. For one fixed graph $G$ it holds for every $k$ above a bound that depends on $G$, primes included. The main tool is a master theorem for a finite abelian group $\Gamma$ with a subgroup $B$ and a set of steps. It gives the connectivity of the flow graph $F(G,\Gamma)$ for every finite abelian group $\Gamma$ that is not cyclic of prime-power order and has a subgroup of order at least $4$ and index at least $10$, for example every abelian group of order $40$.

papers.title: The Exact Nef-Curve Cone Formula for dlt Pairs
papers.abstract: We prove an exact rational-curve formula for the nef-curve cone of every complex projective dlt pair with effective real boundary, answering the related question proposed by Cascini. Every $(K_X+\Delta)$-negative extremal ray is generated by a movable rational curve whose normalization is free in the smooth locus. We reduce the klt case to known results and treat the remaining limiting rays with a new argument based on an orthogonal movable divisor and induction on dimension.

papers.title: The Gvozdenović–Laurent neighborhood bound for the stability number
papers.abstract: We prove the neighborhood bound conjectured by Gvozdenović and Laurent for the copositive sum-of-squares hierarchy for the stability number. One way to bound the size of a stable set is to fix \(r\) of its vertices in all possible ways and use the level-zero relaxation to bound how many more vertices can be added in each case. We prove that level \(r\) of the hierarchy on the original graph already certifies the upper bound obtained by combining all these cases. To combine the local certificates, we view the chosen stable sets as cliques in the complement and take a weighted sum over their vertex orderings. A vertex-deletion identity then lets us reduce the clique size one step at a time while preserving a sum-of-squares certificate. The resulting certificate belongs to the smaller cone of Peña, Vera, and Zuluaga. As a consequence, if a graph has stability number \(\alpha\ge 2\) and no single edge deletion increases \(\alpha\), then level \(\alpha-2\) is exact, one level earlier than the general guarantee.

papers.title: The inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for groups of Lie type C
papers.abstract: We prove the inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for the symplectic groups. A key result is the determination of the character fields of the irreducible characters of the extensions of the symplectic group by field automorphisms. Two main ingredients for this are the theory of Brauer trees and the generalized Gelfand-Graev characters.

papers.title: The irreducibility of tame character varieties
papers.abstract: Tame character varieties are known to be irreducible when the parametrised local systems have monodromies lying in closures of generic conjugacy classes; we will establish their irreducibility without the genericity assumption. A combination of nonabelian Hodge correspondence and variation of parabolic weights reduces the problem to the case of almost generic semi-simple monodromies, which is then treated using a point-counting result of Scognamiglio for nongeneric character stacks. The connectedness result is then used to clarify a couple of facts concerning the symplectic leaves.

papers.title: The natural boundary of the filtered prime-pair Dirichlet series
papers.abstract: Let $p$ and $p'$ range independently over the primes. We prove that the filtered prime-pair Dirichlet series \[ T_0(s)=\sum_{p,p'}\frac{\log p\,\log p'}{(p+p')^s} \left(1-s+s(s+1)\frac{pp'}{(p+p')^2}\right) \] has a meromorphic continuation to $\Re s>1$ with natural boundary $\Re s=1$. We assume $H_\infty$, which says that for every $\epsilon>0$ only finitely many nontrivial zeta zeros have real part greater than $1/2+\epsilon$, together with classical facts about $\zeta$ and $\Gamma$: symmetries and counts of the zeros, a local expansion of $\zeta'/\zeta$, Littlewood's gap estimate and Stirling's formula on strips. The polynomial factor comes from applying the operator $1+x\,d/dx$ to the exponential sum $\sum_p(\log p)\mathrm{e}^{-px}$, which removes its main term $x^{-1}$ as $x\to0$. This removes the pairing of the pole of the prime Dirichlet series at $1$ with zeta zeros divided by primes, which gives the known boundary of the unfiltered series. A term from the prime squares and a remainder survive beside the sum over zeros, and squaring the expansion produces pairs of zeros $\rho,\rho'$ themselves, with complex weights carrying the factor $(\rho-1)(\rho'-1)$. Several pairs can have the same sum, and their weights could cancel there. A sector theorem for weighted Gamma products, proved in a companion paper, shows that they do not cancel at a sum of bounded imaginary part that has at least one representation, provided both zeros of every representation have sufficiently large absolute ordinates. If infinitely many zeros lie off the critical line, this gives poles in $\Re s>1$ that approach every point of the line $\Re s=1$. If only finitely many do, we move the pairs involving those zeros into a correction term. The remaining pair sum, multiplied by the distance to $\Re s=1$, then has a nonzero limit from the right at a dense set of points of that line. The Lean formalization takes the classical inputs as explicit premises.

papers.title: The primitive balanced-degree spectrum in the two-pair Image problem
papers.abstract: Over every characteristic-zero field, the balanced degrees admitting radially primitive, absolutely nonpower two-pair Image counterexamples are precisely $4,6,7,8,\ldots$. All pure balanced phases through degree three are safe, as are all pure radially primitive balanced quintics. One explicit integer family realizes the failure degrees with a common marker of balanced degree one that detects every positive power. We also prove that an abelian variety with Rosati-compatible rank-two multiplication by a CM field has ordinary primes of density one after finite extension if at most two conjugate embedding pairs have Hodge multiplicities $(1,1)$. The full geometric endomorphism algebra may be larger than the acting field. In the quintic proof, this theorem supplies ordinary reduction for factors of cyclic covers whose Frobenius coefficients detect nonzero polynomial moments.

papers.title: The tensor rank of the permanent
papers.abstract: We prove that the ordinary tensor rank of the $n\times n$ permanent, with one factor for each row, is $2^{n-1}$ over every field of characteristic different from two. Every shortest decomposition for $n\ge3$ is Glynn's sign formula up to diagonal changes of variables and rescaling of the factors in each summand. In characteristic two the rank is strictly larger for $n\ge3$. More generally, the rank of the multilinear map computing all square-free coefficients of a product of $k$ linear forms in $n$ variables is $\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}\binom{n}{k-2j}$ in characteristic different from two. The proof evaluates arbitrary rank-one summands on subsets of the input slots. A quadratic relation acts injectively on one evaluation space and maps it into the kernel of the next multiplication map. Iteration gives the lower bound. Character interpolation attains it and extends the formula to uniform higher truncations.

papers.title: The type I conjecture for locally compact groups acting on trees
papers.abstract: We prove that a closed group of automorphisms acting minimally on a locally finite tree and two-transitively on its boundary is uniformly admissible, hence of type I. This solves Nebbia's conjecture in a strong form. Together with the work of Caprace, Kalantar and Monod, this shows that for every closed nonamenable subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(T)$ acting minimally on a locally finite tree $T$, $G$ is of type I if and only if the action on $\partial T$ is two-transitive. The key ingredient is the following operator algebraic result: if the projections of two atomic von Neumann algebras $A_1, A_2$ have integer traces, then every amenable amalgamated free product $A_1 \ast_B A_2$ with $B$ atomic is of type I.

papers.title: The Zilber–Pink conjecture for algebraic tori
papers.abstract: We prove the full Zilber--Pink conjecture for algebraic tori over $\mathbb C$. For every irreducible complex subvariety $X\subseteq \mathbb{G}_m^n$, the intersections of $X$ with torsion cosets have only finitely many maximal atypical components relative to the smallest torsion coset containing $X$. More precisely, $X$ has only finitely many optimal subvarieties. The proof first establishes non-density over $\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$ in a fixed height neighborhood of the algebraic subgroups of codimension greater than $\dim X$, under the hypothesis that $X$ lies in no proper algebraic subgroup. Specialization then gives the exact intersection statement over $\mathbb C$.

papers.title: Transfer principles for Galois cohomology and Serre's conjecture II
papers.abstract:
In this article, we prove several transfer principles for the cohomological dimension of fields. Given a fixed field $K$ with finite cohomological dimension $\delta$, the two main ones allow to:
  - construct totally ramified extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq \delta - 1$ when $K$ is a complete discrete valuation field;
  - construct algebraic extensions of $K$ with cohomological dimension $\leq \delta-1$ and satisfying a norm condition.
  We then apply these results to Serre's conjecture II and to some variants for fields of any cohomological dimension that are inspired by conjectures of Kato and Kuzumaki. In particular, we prove that Serre's conjecture II for characteristic $0$ fields implies Serre's conjecture II for positive characteristic fields.

papers.title: Turán's Hermite strip problem (1967) is resolved: the sharp half-width is 0.90366…
papers.abstract: Turán asked whether a single strip |Im z| ≤ c contains a zero of every polynomial 1 + 2z + aH_n(z) + bH_m(z), where H_j is the jth Hermite polynomial (normalized so that H_1(z) = 2z), 2 ≤ n < m, and a, b are arbitrary complex numbers. The question appeared in Hayman's 1967 collection of research problems. For trinomials (b = 0), Makai and Turán proved that such a strip exists, and Schmeisser found its least half-width, 0.52891952…, in 1971. For the full family we prove that such a strip exists and find its least half-width, 0.903669747226… = (√3/2) cosh(log(1 + √2)/3). Only two of these polynomials have no zero in the open strip of this half-width: a cubic with a triple zero, and the cubic obtained by conjugating its coefficients a and b. For every pair (n, m) other than (2, 3), each such polynomial has a zero in the open strip |Im z| < 9/10. A compactness argument, without computation, shows that some disk |z| < R, and so a strip, contains a zero of every such polynomial; this alone answers Turán's question, but it gives no value of R. The proof of the exact constant combines analytic bounds with exact arithmetic certificates for finitely many cases; the analytic bounds are proved in the paper, and the certificates and the programs that check them are given in a supplement [1]. These results are verified in Lean.

papers.title: Turán's Hermite strip problem (1967) is resolved: the sharp half-width is 0.90366…, and other miscellanea
papers.abstract: Turán asked whether a single strip |Im z| ≤ c contains a zero of every polynomial 1 + 2z + aH_n(z) + bH_m(z), where H_j is the jth Hermite polynomial (normalized so that H_1(z) = 2z), 2 ≤ n < m, and a, b are arbitrary complex numbers. The question appeared in Hayman's 1967 collection of research problems. For trinomials (b = 0), Makai and Turán proved that such a strip exists, and Schmeisser found its least half-width, 0.52891952…, in 1971. For the full family we prove that such a strip exists and find its least half-width, 0.903669747226… = (√3/2) cosh(log(1 + √2)/3). Only two of these polynomials have no zero in the open strip of this half-width: a cubic with a triple zero, and the cubic obtained by conjugating its coefficients a and b. If the index pair (2, 3) is excluded, the least half-width is 0.87004537354988…, attained by exactly two conjugate quintics. A compactness argument, without computation, shows that some disk |z| < R, and so a strip, contains a zero of every such polynomial; this alone answers Turán's question, but it gives no value of R. The proof of the exact constant combines analytic bounds with exact arithmetic certificates for finitely many cases; the analytic bounds are proved in the paper, and the certificates and the programs that check them are given in a supplement [1]. The numbered results outside Section 5 and Appendix A.5 are verified in Lean.

papers.title: Uniform lower bound of arithmetic Hilbert--Samuel function of hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we give an explicit and uniform lower bound for the arithmetic Hilbert--Samuel function of projective hypersurfaces in the framework of Arakelov geometry. The bound has optimal dependence on the height of the varieties. As an application, we use this lower bound to study the determinant method.

papers.title: Uniform Quantum Fourier Transforms from Fast Integer Multiplication
papers.abstract: We construct a polynomial-time uniform family of unitary circuits for the \(q\)-qubit quantum Fourier transform (QFT). For fixed or inverse-polynomial error and every fixed \(\delta>0\), the circuits use \(O_\delta(q(\log\log q)^{1/2+\delta})\) elementary Clifford and \(T\) gates in total, including the gates needed to prepare and uncompute auxiliary registers. We obtain this bound by implementing OpenAI’s November 2026 integer multiplication algorithm as a uniform Boolean circuit and reusing a single phase-gradient register for the product phases and leaf rotations in the QFT recursion of Kayal, Mittal, Paraashar, and Saurabh. We also resolve their uniformity question by giving a deterministic classical algorithm that computes the rotation angle in their exact circuit to additive error \(2^{-d}\) in time polynomial in \(q\) and \(d\). Finally, with intermediate measurements and unit-cost exact dyadic phase gates, we combine one product phase with a semiclassical Fourier measurement to implement the exact QFT using \(O(M(q)+q)\) gates and measurements on every branch, where \(M(q)\) is the Boolean circuit size for multiplying two \(q\)-bit integers.

papers.title: Weitzenbeock's theorem in arbitrary characteristic
papers.abstract: Let \(k\) be a field and \(V\) a finite-dimensional rational representation of the additive group \(\GG_{a,k}\). We show that the ring of invariants \(k[V]^{\GG_a}\) is finitely generated in every characteristic, extending Weitzenb\"ock's classical theorem beyond characteristic zero.

papers.title: When $D$-companion matrix meets Sendov's conjecture
papers.abstract: Sendov's conjecture is a longstanding problem in the geometry of polynomials. It was recently proved by Lech Mazur. Terence Tao subsequently presented a simplified proof on his blog. Both proofs, however, rely on computer-assisted verification for intermediate degrees. Following Tao's framework, we give a new proof based on the $D$-companion matrix that requires no computer-assisted verification. The key difference lies in treating the ranges $0<\alpha\leq3$ and $\alpha\geq3$ separately, where $\alpha=(n-1)(1-|a|^2)/2$ and $a$ is the zero under consideration. This enables us to replace the finite verification with uniform analytic estimates valid for all degrees.

papers.title: Wilson primes for the ring of functions regular outside a rational point of a curve
papers.abstract: Let C be a smooth projective curve over F_q, infinity a rational point and A the ring of functions regular outside infinity. For a basis of A adapted to the pole order at infinity we consider the Wilson product W_d of Hexagon 2611.01011 and 2611.01053 and prove, without any plane model, that for every prime element pi of degree d, W_d = -1 + pi Theta/(d pi)^2 mod pi^2, where Theta = sum_j dm_j nu_j, (m_j) is the basis of the space of representatives and (nu_j) the dual basis of differentials for the residue pairing. We then show that, for a Cauchy kernel kappa on C x C of order at most 2g-1 (one always exists), Theta = E_kappa(pi) + K_pi d pi, where E_kappa is a second order differential operator attached to kappa and K_pi a differential defined by a decomposition involving at most g basis elements. This contains Thakur's criterion for F_q[t] and the theorems of the two notes above for plane curves. As a case not covered by these, we treat a hyperelliptic curve in odd characteristic with infinity an affine rational point where y is not zero, with an explicit kernel; there the correction K_pi is a single differential.

papers.title: Working Backwards from the Formal Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis: Mathematical Discovery by Navigating Evolving Relational Topologies
papers.abstract: The AI-assisted formal proof of the Riemann hypothesis released in 2026 raises fundamental questions about the future of mathematics. Mathematical proofs may increasingly exceed the length, complexity, and other limits within which human mathematicians can independently validate, reconstruct, or understand them using existing tools. Could AI eventually produce mathematics faster than humans can meaningfully contribute to it? Could the proliferation of mathematical objects whose generative relationships cannot be reconstructed threaten the functional coherence of mathematics as a collectively navigable body of knowledge? Or could these developments instead signal the beginning of a fundamentally different mathematics? This paper investigates these questions by proposing a general functional model of mathematical information and identifying a potential systematic blind spot in mathematical discovery. The central hypothesis is that any human or artificial mathematical observer lacking a model of information with adequate functional and energetic closure may be unable to systematically distinguish between two classes of mathematical operations: local coherence (L) operations, composed through direct relationships among sufficiently known functions and operands using functional information that is complete with respect to the targeted problem; and global coherence (G) operations, composed or generated through potentially indirect relationships among partially known functions and operands using partial functional information and recursive assessment. Where discovering a mathematical object requires generating or correcting relationships outside an observer's existing operative closure, that observer may correctly execute its available mathematics while remaining systematically unable to discover the object. The distinction concerns two different mathematical capabilities: navigating relationships that are already operable, and discovering the dynamics through which new relationships become operable. The proposed functional model represents mathematical information within an evolving mathematical information space (M-space), in which mathematical objects, operators, assessments, histories, corrections, and their functional work requirements become operands of further mathematical operations. Functional and energetic closure provide the proposed conditions for recursively navigating and correcting these relationships under finite available work. Mathematical discovery can consequently be investigated as navigation through a target-relative fitness landscape whose operative topology may itself change through discovery. A further M-Tower conjecture investigates whether embedding the same representation of mathematical information into every dimension N (collectively the M-Tower of M-space) creates a series of representations capable of together representing any geometric, topological, algebraic, and calculational relationships through recursively composable mathematical structures across dimensions. The model predicts that a second-order model of information (one with an explicit model of itself through which it can correct itself) can combinatorially with each use and exponentially in total, expand the navigability and discoverability of mathematical information, as well as capacity to make mathematics understandable to humans. Prior work has developed representation-changing and operator-generating methods for substantial classes of problems; the additional conjecture here is that a single recursively correctable, functionally and energetically closed infrastructure can support these discovery dynamics across mathematical and other functional domains. Working backwards from the documented Riemann hypothesis proof, this paper investigates these predictions. The established bounded results demonstrate conditions under which mathematical information is lost or recovered and previously unavailable mathematical continuations become operable. Finally, the model identifies and strongly types mathematical contributions humans can currently make, including cross-domain functional-pattern discovery, generation of mathematical relationships, global-coherence assessment, and transmission of reconstructible mathematical understanding. It also identifies functional and energetic conditions under which future human contributions may remain unavailable to particular artificial systems. The resulting implication is not that mathematics is ending for humans, but that a new and very different mathematics may be beginning.

papers.title: Zero-cycles and holomorphic forms in families
papers.abstract: We establish parallel Chow and Hodge-theoretic rigidity theorems for dominant projective morphisms between smooth complex varieties. For instance, if the general fiber satisfies $CH_0(F) = \mathbb{Z}$, then the same is true of every fiber. Similarly, if the general fiber is connected with $H^0(F, \Omega_F^p) = 0$ for $p > 0$, then the same is true of every fiber. This extends the case of rationally connected fibrations from [Bur26]. We further introduce higher Chow-theoretic notions of singularities.
